verses.sa: अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् । महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥ २२॥
verses.iast: aśarīram̐ śarīreṣvanavastheṣvavasthitam । mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ॥ 22॥
verses.tr: The intelligent one having known the Self to be bodiless in (all) bodies, to be firmly seated in things that are perishable, and to be great and all-pervading, does not grieve.

verses.sa: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूꣳ स्वाम् ॥ २३॥
verses.iast: nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena । yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūꣳ svām ॥ 23॥
verses.tr: The Self cannot be attained by the study of the Vedas, not by intelligence nor by much hearing. Only by him who seeks to know the Self can It be attained. To him the Self reveals Its own nature.

verses.sa: नाविरतो दुश्चरितान्नाशान्तो नासमाहितः । नाशान्तमानसो वाऽपि प्रज्ञानेनैनमाप्नुयात् ॥ २४॥
verses.iast: nāvirato duścaritānnāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ । nāśāntamānaso vā’pi prajñānenainamāpnuyāt ॥ 24॥
verses.tr: None who has not refrained from bad conduct, whose senses are not under restraint, whose mind is not collected or who does not preserve a tranquil mind, can attain this Self through knowledge.

verses.sa: यस्य ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं च उभे भवत ओदनः । मृत्युर्यस्योपसेचनं क इत्था वेद यत्र सः ॥ २५॥
verses.iast: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ । mṛtyuryasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ ॥ 25॥
verses.tr: The Self to which both the Brahmana and the Kshatriya are food, (as it were), and Death a soup, how can one know thus where It is.

verses.sa: ऋतं पिबन्तौ सुकृतस्य लोके गुहां प्रविष्टौ परमे परार्धे । छायातपौ ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति पञ्चाग्नयो ये च त्रिणाचिकेताः ॥ १॥
verses.iast: ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe । chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: The knowers of Brahman and those who kindle the five fires and propitiate the Nachiketa Fire thrice, speak of as light and shade, the two that enjoy the results of righteous deeds, entering within the body, into the innermost cavity (of the heart), the supreme abode (of Brahman).

verses.sa: यः सेतुरीजानानामक्षरं ब्रह्म यत् परम् । अभयं तितीर्षतां पारं नाचिकेतँ शकेमहि ॥ २॥
verses.iast: yaḥ seturījānānāmakṣaraṃ brahma yat param । abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketam̐ śakemahi ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: May we be able to know the Nachiketa Fire which is the bridge for the sacrificers, as also the imperishable Brahman, fearless, as well as the other shore for those who are desirous of crossing (the ocean of samsara).

verses.sa: आत्मानँ रथिनं विद्धि शरीरँ रथमेव तु । बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: ātmānam̐ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīram̐ rathameva tu । buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: Know the Self to be the master of the chariot, and the body to be the chariot. Know the intellect to be the charioteer, and the mind to be the reins.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयाँ स्तेषु गोचरान् । आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: indriyāṇi hayānāhurviṣayām̐ steṣu gocarān । ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: The senses they speak of as the horses; the objects within their view, the way. When the Self is yoked with the mind and the senses, the wise call It the enjoyer.

verses.sa: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: yastvavijñānavānbhavatyayuktena manasā sadā । tasyendriyāṇyavaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: But whoso is devoid of discrimination and is possessed of a mind ever uncollected – his senses are uncontrollable like the vicious horses of a driver.

verses.sa: यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: yastu vijñānavānbhavati yuktena manasā sadā । tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: But whoso is discriminative and possessed of a mind ever collected – his senses are controllable like the good horses of a driver.

verses.sa: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्यमनस्कः सदाऽशुचिः । न स तत्पदमाप्नोति संसारं चाधिगच्छति ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: yastvavijñānavānbhavatyamanaskaḥ sadā’śuciḥ । na sa tatpadamāpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: But whoso is devoid of a discriminating intellect, possessed of an unrestrained mind and is ever impure, does not attain that goal, but goes to samsara.

verses.sa: यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति समनस्कः सदा शुचिः । स तु तत्पदमाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: yastu vijñānavānbhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ । sa tu tatpadamāpnoti yasmādbhūyo na jāyate ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: But whoso is possessed of a discriminating intellect and a restrained mind, and is ever pure, attains that goal from which he is not born again.

verses.sa: विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनः प्रग्रहवान्नरः । सोऽध्वनः पारमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: vijñānasārathiryastu manaḥ pragrahavānnaraḥ । so’dhvanaḥ pāramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: But the man who has a discriminating intellect as his driver, and a controlled-mind as the reins, reaches the end of the path – that supreme state of Vishnu.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यश्च परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान्परः ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: indriyebhyaḥ parā hyarthā arthebhyaśca paraṃ manaḥ । manasastu parā buddhirbuddherātmā mahānparaḥ ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: The sensory objects are subtler than the senses, and subtler than the sensory objects is mind. But intellect is subtler than mind and subtler than intellect is Mahat (the Hiranyagarbha).

verses.sa: महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः । पुरुषान्न परं किंचित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ । puruṣānna paraṃ kiṃcitsā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: The unmanifested (avyakta) is subtler than Mahat (Hiranyagarbha) and subtler than the unmanifested is Purusha. There is nothing subtler than Purusha. That is the end, that is the supreme goal.

verses.sa: एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽऽत्मा न प्रकाशते । दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः ॥ १२॥
verses.iast: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho’’tmā na prakāśate । dṛśyate tvagryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ ॥ 12॥
verses.tr: This Self hidden in all beings does not shine. But by seers of subtle and pointed intellect capable of perceiving subtle objects, It is seen.

verses.sa: यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञस्तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञान आत्मनि । ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेत्तद्यच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि ॥ १३॥
verses.iast: yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñastadyacchejjñāna ātmani । jñānamātmani mahati niyacchettadyacchecchānta ātmani ॥ 13॥
verses.tr: Let the wise man merge speech in his mind, merge that (mind) into the intelligent self and the intelligent self into the Mahat. (Let him then) merge the Mahat into the peaceful Self.

verses.sa: उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत । क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥ १४॥
verses.iast: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varānnibodhata । kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathastatkavayo vadanti ॥ 14॥
verses.tr: Arise, awake, and learn by approaching the exalted ones, for that path is sharp as a razor’s edge, impassable, and hard to go by, say the wise.

verses.sa: अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथाऽरसं नित्यमगन्धवच्च यत् । अनाद्यनन्तं महतः परं ध्रुवं निचाय्य तन्मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते ॥ १५॥
verses.iast: aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayaṃ tathā’rasaṃ nityamagandhavacca yat । anādyanantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tanmṛtyumukhāt pramucyate ॥ 15॥
verses.tr: By knowing that which is soundless, touchless, formless, undecaying, so also tasteless, eternal, odorless, beginningless, endless, subtler than Mahat and constant, man is liberated from the jaws of death.

verses.sa: नाचिकेतमुपाख्यानं मृत्युप्रोक्तँ सनातनम् । उक्त्वा श्रुत्वा च मेधावी ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ १६॥
verses.iast: nāciketamupākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktam̐ sanātanam । uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate ॥ 16॥
verses.tr: Narrating and hearing this eternal story of Nachiketas told by Death, the intelligent man attains glory in the world of Brahman.

verses.sa: य इमं परमं गुह्यं श्रावयेद् ब्रह्मसंसदि । प्रयतः श्राद्धकाले वा तदानन्त्याय कल्पते । तदानन्त्याय कल्पत इति ॥ १७॥
verses.iast: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi । prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tadānantyāya kalpate । tadānantyāya kalpata iti ॥ 17॥
verses.tr: Whoso, becoming pure, causes this supreme secret to be recited before am assembly of the Brahmanas, or at the time of Sraddha, that (ceremony) secures for him infinite results, secures infinite results.

verses.sa: पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयम्भूस्तस्मात्पराङ्पश्यति नान्तरात्मन् । कश्चिद्धीरः प्रत्यगात्मानमैक्षदावृत्तचक्षुरमृतत्वमिच्छन् ॥ १॥
verses.iast: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayambhūstasmātparāṅpaśyati nāntarātman । kaściddhīraḥ pratyagātmānamaikṣadāvṛttacakṣuramṛtatvamicchan ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: The self-existent damned the out-going senses. Therefore one sees externally and not the internal Self. Someone (who is) intelligent, with his eyes turned away, desirous of immortality, sees the inner Self.

verses.sa: पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् । अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ॥ २॥
verses.iast: parācaḥ kāmānanuyanti bālāste mṛtyoryanti vitatasya pāśam । atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvamadhruveṣviha na prārthayante ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: The unintelligent go after outward pleasures; they fall into the meshes of wide-spread death. But the intelligent, having known immortality to be constant, never covet here objects that are inconstant.

verses.sa: येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान् स्पर्शाꣳश्च मैथुनान् । एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśāꣳśca maithunān । etenaiva vijānāti kimatra pariśiṣyate । etadvai tat ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: By the self (a man knows) form, taste, odor, sound, touch, and the sexual joy. What remains here (unknowable to the Self)? This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तं चोभौ येनानुपश्यति । महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati । mahāntaṃ vibhumātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: Knowing that great and all-pervading Self by which one sees (the objects) both in the sleep and the waking states, the intelligent man grieves no more.

verses.sa: य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात् । ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvamantikāt । īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate । etadvai tat ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: Whoso knows the self closely, the honey-eater, the supporter of the vital airs and the lord of the past and the future, will not henceforward protect himself. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत । गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तं यो भूतेभिर्व्यपश्यत । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātamadbhyaḥ pūrvamajāyata । guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhirvyapaśyata । etadvai tat ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: He who perceives the First-born that came into being from Tapas (Brahman) before the waters, and that, entering into the cavity of the heart, is seated there, he perceives that very Brahman. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: या प्राणेन संभवत्यदितिर्देवतामयी । गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: yā prāṇena saṃbhavatyaditirdevatāmayī । guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhirvyajāyata । etadvai tat ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: (He who perceives) this Aditi that comes into being as the Prana, comprising all the gods, that is manifested along with the elements, and that, entering into the cavity of the heart, is seated there, he perceives that very Brahman. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः । दिवे दिवे ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ । dive dive īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadbhirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ । etadvai tat ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: The (sacrificial) fire lodged in the two aranis, even as the foetus is carefully borne by the pregnant woman, is fit to be worshipped every day by men who are wakeful and possessed of oblation. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: यतश्चोदेति सूर्योऽस्तं यत्र च गच्छति । तं देवाः सर्वेऽर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: yataścodeti sūryo’staṃ yatra ca gacchati । taṃ devāḥ sarve’rpitāstadu nātyeti kaścana । etadvai tat ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: On that from which the sun rises and in which it sets, are fixed all the gods. None ever goes beyond that. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह । मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: yadeveha tadamutra yadamutra tadanviha । mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: What indeed is here is there; what is there is here again. Whoso here sees as though different, passes from death to death.

verses.sa: मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानाऽस्ति किंचन । मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: manasaivedamāptavyaṃ neha nānā’sti kiṃcana । mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: By mind alone is this attainable; there is no difference here whatsoever. Whoso here sees as though different, passes from death to death.

verses.sa: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति । ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते । एतद्वै तत् ॥ १२॥
verses.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati । īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate । etadvai tat ॥ 12॥
verses.tr: The Purusha, of the size of a thumb, dwells in the body. (Realizing Him as) the Lord of the past and the future, one does not (henceforward) want to protect oneself. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिवाधूमकः । ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः । एतद्वै तत् ॥ १३॥
verses.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotirivādhūmakaḥ । īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ । etadvai tat ॥ 13॥
verses.tr: The Purusha of the size of a thumb is like a smokeless flame and is the Lord of the past and the future. He certainly exists now and shall certainly exist tomorrow. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: यथोदकं दुर्गे वृष्टं पर्वतेषु विधावति । एवं धर्मान् पृथक् पश्यंस्तानेवानुविधावति ॥ १४॥
verses.iast: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati । evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃstānevānuvidhāvati ॥ 14॥
verses.tr: As rain-water fallen on a mountain ridge runs down the rocks, so does one seeing the selves differently run after them alone.

verses.sa: यथोदकं शुद्धे शुद्धमासिक्तं तादृगेव भवति । एवं मुनेर्विजानत आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥ १५॥
verses.iast: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddhamāsiktaṃ tādṛgeva bhavati । evaṃ munervijānata ātmā bhavati gautama ॥ 15॥
verses.tr: As pure water poured into pure water remains the same only, so does the Self of the thinker who knows thus become, O Gautama.

verses.sa: पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः । अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते । एतद्वै तत् ॥ १॥
verses.iast: puramekādaśadvāramajasyāvakracetasaḥ । anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaśca vimucyate । etadvai tat ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: The city of the unborn whose knowledge is like the light of the sun, consists of eleven gates. Meditating on Him, one does not grieve and, becoming free (from bondage), one becomes liberated. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: हँसः शुचिषद्वसुरन्तरिक्षसद्होता वेदिषदतिथिर्दुरोणसत् । नृषद्वरसदृतसद्व्योमसद् अब्जा गोजा ऋतजा अद्रिजा ऋतं बृहत् ॥ २॥
verses.iast: ham̐saḥ śuciṣadvasurantarikṣasadhotā vediṣadatithirduroṇasat । nṛṣadvarasadṛtasadvyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: As mover (sun), He dwells in heaven; (as air), He pervades everything and dwells in inter-space; as fire, on the earth; as guest, in the houses; He dwells in men; dwells in the gods; dwells in truth and dwells in space. He is all that is born in water, all that is born on earth, all that is born in sacrifices and all that is born on the mountains; He is unchanging and great.

verses.sa: ऊर्ध्वं प्राणमुन्नयत्यपानं प्रत्यगस्यति । मध्ये वामनमासीनं विश्वे देवा उपासते ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇamunnayatyapānaṃ pratyagasyati । madhye vāmanamāsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: (He) raises the prana upward and casts the apana downward. All the gods worship Him who is adorable and seated in the middle.

verses.sa: अस्य विस्रंसमानस्य शरीरस्थस्य देहिनः । देहाद्विमुच्यमानस्य किमत्र परिशिष्यते । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ । dehādvimucyamānasya kimatra pariśiṣyate । etadvai tat ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: When this Self seated in the body is torn away and freed from the body, what remains here? This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: न प्राणेन नापानेन मर्त्यो जीवति कश्चन । इतरेण तु जीवन्ति यस्मिन्नेतावुपाश्रितौ ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana । itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminnetāvupāśritau ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: Not by prana, not by apana does a mortal live; but all live by something else on which these two depend.

verses.sa: हन्त त इदं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुह्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् । यथा च मरणं प्राप्य आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam । yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: I will describe to thee, O Gautama, this secret ancient Brahman and also what becomes of the Self after death.

verses.sa: योनिमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते शरीरत्वाय देहिनः । स्थाणुमन्येऽनुसंयन्ति यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम् ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: yonimanye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ । sthāṇumanye’nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: Some jivas enter the womb for assuming bodies; others go into the unmoving, in accordance with their karma and with their knowledge.

verses.sa: य एष सुप्तेषु जागर्ति कामं कामं पुरुषो निर्मिमाणः । तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते । तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत् ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ । tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate । tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana । etadvai tat ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: This Purusha who is awake when all are asleep, creating all things cherished, is certainly pure; that is Brahman; that is called the Immortal. All worlds are strung on that; none passes beyond that. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: अग्निर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: agniryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva । ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: Just as fire, though one, having entered the world, assumes a separate form in respect of every form, so does the in-dwelling Self of all beings, though one, assume a form in respect of every form, and is outside it.

verses.sa: वायुर्यथैको भुवनं प्रविष्टो रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: vāyuryathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva । ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiśca ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: Just as wind, though one, having entered the world, assumes a separate form in respect of each form, so does the in-dwelling Self of all beings, though one, assumes a form in respect of every form and is outside it.

verses.sa: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣuḥ na lipyate cākṣuṣairbāhyadoṣaiḥ । ekastathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: Just as the sun, which is the eye of the entire world, is not tainted by the external impurities seen by the eyes, so also, the in-dwelling Self of all beings, though one, is not tainted by the sorrows of the world, It being external.

verses.sa: एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा एकं रूपं बहुधा यः करोति । तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीराः तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषाम् ॥ १२॥
verses.iast: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti । tamātmasthaṃ ye’nupaśyanti dhīrāḥ teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ॥ 12॥
verses.tr: Eternal happiness belongs to the intelligent – not to others – who realize in their hearts Him who is one, the controller and the in-dwelling Self of all beings, and who makes the one form manifold.

verses.sa: नित्योऽनित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानाम् एको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् । तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यन्ति धीराः तेषां शान्तिः शाश्वती नेतरेषाम् ॥ १३॥
verses.iast: nityo’nityānāṃ cetanaścetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān । tamātmasthaṃ ye’nupaśyanti dhīrāḥ teṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ॥ 13॥
verses.tr: Whoso among the intelligent realize the Self in the (inner space of the) heart as the eternal among the ephemeral, the consciousness among the conscious, who, though one, dispenses the desired objects to many, to them belongs eternal peace, not to others.

verses.sa: तदेतदिति मन्यन्तेऽनिर्देश्यं परमं सुखम् । कथं नु तद्विजानीयां किमु भाति विभाति वा ॥ १४॥
verses.iast: tadetaditi manyante’nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham । kathaṃ nu tadvijānīyāṃ kimu bhāti vibhāti vā ॥ 14॥
verses.tr: How shall I know that indescribable and supreme Bliss which they think of as ‘This’? Is It selfluminous or does It shine distinctly, (making Itself perceptible to the intellect), or does It not?

verses.sa: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥ १५॥
verses.iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto’yamagniḥ । tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ॥ 15॥
verses.tr: There the sun shines not, nor do the moon and the stars, nor do these lightnings. How (then) can this fire (shine)? Everything shines after Him that shines. By His light shines all this.

verses.sa: ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः । तदेव शुक्रं तद्ब्रह्म तदेवामृतमुच्यते । तस्मिँल्लोकाः श्रिताः सर्वे तदु नात्येति कश्चन । एतद्वै तत् ॥ १॥
verses.iast: ūrdhvamūlo’vākśākha eṣo’śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ । tadeva śukraṃ tadbrahma tadevāmṛtamucyate । tasmim̐llokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tadu nātyeti kaścana । etadvai tat ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: This peepul tree with root above and branches down is eternal. That (which is its source) is certainly pure; that is Brahman and that is called immortal. On that are strung all the worlds; none passes beyond that. This verily is that (thou seekest).

verses.sa: यदिदं किं च जगत् सर्वं प्राण एजति निःसृतम् । महद्भयं वज्रमुद्यतं य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥ २॥
verses.iast: yadidaṃ kiṃ ca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam । mahadbhayaṃ vajramudyataṃ ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: All this universe, evolved (from Brahman), moves in prana (in Brahman); the most frightful like an uplifted thunderbolt. Those who know this become immortal.

verses.sa: भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः । भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: bhayādasyāgnistapati bhayāttapati sūryaḥ । bhayādindraśca vāyuśca mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: For fear of Him, fire burns; For fear of Him, shines the sun; For fear of Him, Indra and Vayu function; For fear of Him, death, the fifth, stalks on the earth.

verses.sa: इह चेदशकद्बोद्धुं प्राक्शरीरस्य विस्रसः । ततः सर्गेषु लोकेषु शरीरत्वाय कल्पते ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: iha cedaśakadboddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ । tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: If one could know here prior to the falling of the body, (one becomes liberated); (if not), one becomes fit to be embodied in the worlds of creatures.

verses.sa: यथाऽऽदर्शे तथाऽऽत्मनि यथा स्वप्ने तथा पितृलोके । यथाऽप्सु परीव ददृशे तथा गन्धर्वलोके छायातपयोरिव ब्रह्मलोके ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: yathā’’darśe tathā’’tmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke । yathā’psu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayoriva brahmaloke ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: As in a mirror, so in one’s intellect; as in a dream, so in the world of manes; as seen in water, so in the world of the Gandharvas; as in the case of shade and light, so in the world of Brahma.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावमुदयास्तमयौ च यत् । पृथगुत्पद्यमानानां मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvamudayāstamayau ca yat । pṛthagutpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: The intelligent man, having known the different nature of the senses originating separately (from their causes), as also their rising and setting, does not grieve.

verses.sa: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनो मनसः सत्त्वमुत्तमम् । सत्त्वादधि महानात्मा महतोऽव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvamuttamam । sattvādadhi mahānātmā mahato’vyaktamuttamam ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: The mind is subtler than the senses; subtler than the mind is the intellect; Mahat (Hiranyagarbha) is subtler than the intellect; subtler than Mahat is Avyakta (Unmanifested).

verses.sa: अव्यक्तात्तु परः पुरुषो व्यापकोऽलिङ्ग एव च । यं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते जन्तुरमृतत्वं च गच्छति ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: avyaktāttu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako’liṅga eva ca । yaṃ jñātvā mucyate janturamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: But subtler than Avyakta is Purusha, all-pervading and without a linga (distinguishing mark) indeed, knowing whom a mortal becomes freed and attains immortality.

verses.sa: न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनम् । हृदा मनीषा मनसाऽभिकॢप्तो य एतद्विदुरमृतास्ते भवन्ति ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam । hṛdā manīṣā manasā’bhikḷpto ya etadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: His form does not stand within the scope of vision; none beholds Him with the eye. By the intellect restraining the mind, and through meditation is He revealed. Those who know this become immortal.

verses.sa: यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह । बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टते तामाहुः परमां गतिम् ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha । buddhiśca na viceṣṭate tāmāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: When the five senses of knowledge are at rest together with the mind, and the intellect is not active, that state they call the highest.

verses.sa: तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिरामिन्द्रियधारणाम् । अप्रमत्तस्तदा भवति योगो हि प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: tāṃ yogamiti manyante sthirāmindriyadhāraṇām । apramattastadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: That steady restraint over the senses they regard as yoga. Then one becomes vigilant, for yoga can indeed originate (in one) and can be lost (as well).

verses.sa: नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा । अस्तीति ब्रुवतोऽन्यत्र कथं तदुपलभ्यते ॥ १२॥
verses.iast: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā । astīti bruvato’nyatra kathaṃ tadupalabhyate ॥ 12॥
verses.tr: Not by speech, not by mind, not by the eye can It be attained. Except in the case of one who says, ‘It exists’, how can It be known to anyone else?

verses.sa: अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धव्यस्तत्त्वभावेन चोभयोः । अस्तीत्येवोपलब्धस्य तत्त्वभावः प्रसीदति ॥ १३॥
verses.iast: astītyevopalabdhavyastattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ । astītyevopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati ॥ 13॥
verses.tr: The Self should be apprehended as existing and also as It really is. Of these two (aspects), to him who knows It to exist, Its true nature is revealed.

verses.sa: यदा सर्वे प्रमुच्यन्ते कामा येऽस्य हृदि श्रिताः । अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते ॥ १४॥
verses.iast: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye’sya hṛdi śritāḥ । atha martyo’mṛto bhavatyatra brahma samaśnute ॥ 14॥
verses.tr: When all longings that are in the heart vanish, then a mortal becomes immortal and attains Brahman here.

verses.sa: यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः । अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवत्येतावद्ध्यनुशासनम् ॥ १५॥
verses.iast: yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ । atha martyo’mṛto bhavatyetāvaddhyanuśāsanam ॥ 15॥
verses.tr: When all the knots of the heart are cut asunder here, then a mortal becomes immortal. Only this much is the instruction.

verses.sa: शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभिनिःसृतैका । तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति विष्वङ्ङन्या उत्क्रमणे भवन्ति ॥ १६॥
verses.iast: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyastāsāṃ mūrdhānamabhiniḥsṛtaikā । tayordhvamāyannamṛtatvameti viṣvaṅṅanyā utkramaṇe bhavanti ॥ 16॥
verses.tr: There are a hundred and one nerves of the heart. Of then, one goes out piercing the head. Going up through that, one attains immortality; the others serve for departing in different ways.

verses.sa: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोऽन्तरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः । तं स्वाच्छरीरात्प्रवृहेन्मुञ्जादिवेषीकां धैर्येण । तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्छुक्रममृतमिति ॥ १७॥
verses.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo’ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ । taṃ svāccharīrātpravṛhenmuñjādiveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa । taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtaṃ taṃ vidyācchukramamṛtamiti ॥ 17॥
verses.tr: Purusha of the size of a thumb, the inner Self, is ever seated in the heart of all living beings. One should, with steadiness, separate Him from one’s own body as stalk from the Munja grass. One should know Him as pure and immortal; one should know Him as pure and immortal.

verses.sa: मृत्युप्रोक्तां नचिकेतोऽथ लब्ध्वा विद्यामेतां योगविधिं च कृत्स्नम् । ब्रह्मप्राप्तो विरजोऽभूद्विमृत्युरन्योऽप्येवं यो विदध्यात्ममेव ॥ १८॥
verses.iast: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo’tha labdhvā vidyāmetāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam । brahmaprāpto virajo’bhūdvimṛtyuranyo’pyevaṃ yo vidadhyātmameva ॥ 18॥
verses.tr: Nachiketas then, having acquired this knowledge imparted by Death, as also the instructions on Yoga in entirety, attained Brahman having become dispassionate and deathless. So does become any one else also who knows the inner Self thus.

verses.sa: केनेषितं पतति प्रेषितं मनः केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः । केनेषितां वाचमिमां वदन्ति चक्षुः श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ॥
verses.iast: keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ । keneṣitāṃ vācamimāṃ vadanti cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti ॥
verses.tr: Wished by whom is the mind directed to fall (on its objects)? Directed by whom does the foremost vital air move? By whom is wished this speech which the people utter? Who is the radiant being that unites the eye and the ear (with their objects)?

verses.sa: श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रं मनसो मनो यद् वाचो ह वाचं स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः । चक्षुषश्चक्षुरतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
verses.iast: śrotrasya śrotraṃ manaso mano yad vāco ha vācaṃ sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ । cakṣuṣaścakṣuratimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ॥
verses.tr: Because He is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, the vital air of the vital air, and the eye of the eye, the wise, freeing themselves (from the identity with the senses) and renouncing the world, become immortal.

verses.sa: न तत्र चक्षुर्गच्छति न वाग् गच्छति नो मनः । न विद्मो न विजानीमो यथैतदनुशिष्यात् । अन्यदेव तद्विदितादथो अविदितादधि । इति शुश्रुम पूर्वेषां ये नस्तद् व्याचचक्षिरे ॥
verses.iast: na tatra cakṣurgacchati na vāg gacchati no manaḥ । na vidmo na vijānīmo yathaitadanuśiṣyāt । anyadeva tadviditādatho aviditādadhi । iti śuśruma pūrveṣāṃ ye nastad vyācacakṣire ॥
verses.tr: The eye does not reach there, nor speech, nor mind, nor do we know (Its mature). Therefore we don’t know how to impart instruction (about It). Distinct indeed is That from the known and distinct from the unknown. Thus have we heard from the ancients who expounded It to us.

verses.sa: यद्वाचानभ्युदितं येन वागभ्युद्यते । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
verses.iast: yadvācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāgabhyudyate । tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥
verses.tr: That which is not uttered by speech, that by which the word is expressed, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

verses.sa: यन्मनसा न मनुते येनाहुर्मनो मतम् । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
verses.iast: yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano matam । tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥
verses.tr: That which one does not think with the mind, that by which, they say, the mind is thought, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

verses.sa: यच्चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूंषि पश्यति । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
verses.iast: yaccakṣuṣā na paśyati yena cakṣūṃṣi paśyati । tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥
verses.tr: That which man does not see with the eye, that by which man sees the activities of the eye, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

verses.sa: यच्छ्रोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रमिदं श्रुतम् । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
verses.iast: yacchrotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotramidaṃ śrutam । tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥
verses.tr: That which man does not hear with the ear, that by which man hears the ear’s hearing, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

verses.sa: यत्प्राणेन न प्राणिति येन प्राणः प्रणीयते । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥
verses.iast: yatprāṇena na prāṇiti yena prāṇaḥ praṇīyate । tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ॥
verses.tr: That which man does not smell with the organ of smell, that by which the organ of smell is attracted towards its objects, know That alone to be Brahman, and not this (non-Brahman) which is being worshiped.

verses.sa: यदि मन्यसे सुवेदेति दभ्रमेवापि नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपम् । यदस्य त्वं यदस्य देवेष्वथ नु मीमांस्यमेव ते मन्ये विदितम् ॥
verses.iast: yadi manyase suvedeti dabhramevāpi nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpam । yadasya tvaṃ yadasya deveṣvatha nu mīmāṃsyameva te manye viditam ॥
verses.tr: If you think, ‘I know Brahman rightly’, you have known but little of Brahman’s (true) nature. What you know of His form and what form you know among the gods (too is but little). Therefore Brahman is still to be inquired into by you. I think Brahman is known to me.

verses.sa: नाहं मन्ये सुवेदेति नो न वेदेति वेद च । यो नस्तद्वेद तद्वेद नो न वेदेति वेद च ॥
verses.iast: nāhaṃ manye suvedeti no na vedeti veda ca । yo nastadveda tadveda no na vedeti veda ca ॥
verses.tr: I think not I know Brahman rightly, nor do I think It is unknown. I know (and I do not know also). He among us who knows that knows It (Brahman); not that It is not known nor that It is known.

verses.sa: यस्यामतं तस्य मतं मतं यस्य न वेद सः । अविज्ञातं विजानतां विज्ञातमविजानताम् ॥
verses.iast: yasyāmataṃ tasya mataṃ mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ । avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ vijñātamavijānatām ॥
verses.tr: It is known to him to whom It is unknown; he to whom It is known does not know It. It is unknown to those who know, and known to those who know not.

verses.sa: प्रतिबोधविदितं मतममृतत्वं हि विन्दते । आत्मना विन्दते वीर्यं विद्यया विन्दतेऽमृतम् ॥
verses.iast: pratibodhaviditaṃ matamamṛtatvaṃ hi vindate । ātmanā vindate vīryaṃ vidyayā vindate’mṛtam ॥
verses.tr: When Brahman is known as the inner Self (of cognition) in every state of consciousness, It is known in reality, because one thus attains immortality. Through one’s own Self is attained strength and through knowledge is attained immortality.

verses.sa: इह चेदवेदीदथ सत्यमस्ति न चेदिहावेदीन्महती विनष्टिः । भूतेषु भूतेषु विचित्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवन्ति ॥
verses.iast: iha cedavedīdatha satyamasti na cedihāvedīnmahatī vinaṣṭiḥ । bhūteṣu bhūteṣu vicitya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavanti ॥
verses.tr: Here if one has realized, then there is accomplishment. Here if one has not realized, then there is utter ruin. Having realized Brahman in all beings, and having withdrawn from this world, the wise become immortal.

verses.sa: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त । त ऐक्षन्तास्माकमेवायं विजयोऽस्माकमेवायं महिमेति ॥
verses.iast: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta । ta aikṣantāsmākamevāyaṃ vijayo’smākamevāyaṃ mahimeti ॥
verses.tr: It is well-known that Brahman indeed achieved victory for the gods. But in that victory which was Brahman’s the gods reveled in joy.

verses.sa: तद्धैषां विजज्ञौ तेभ्यो ह प्रादुर्बभूव तन्न व्यजानत किमिदं यक्षमिति ॥
verses.iast: taddhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādurbabhūva tanna vyajānata kimidaṃ yakṣamiti ॥
verses.tr: They thought, “Ours alone is this victory, ours alone is this glory”. Brahman knew this their pride and appeared before them, but they knew not who this Yaksha (worshipful Being) was.

verses.sa: तेऽग्निमब्रुवन्जातवेद एतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति ॥
verses.iast: te’gnimabruvanjātaveda etadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti ॥
verses.tr: They said to Agni: “O Jataveda, know thou this as to who this Yaksha is”. (He said:) “So be it.”

verses.sa: तदभ्यद्रवत् तमभ्यवदत् कोऽसीत्यग्निर्वा अहमस्मीत्यब्रवीज्जातवेदा वा अहमस्मीति ॥
verses.iast: tadabhyadravat tamabhyavadat ko’sītyagnirvā ahamasmītyabravījjātavedā vā ahamasmīti ॥
verses.tr: Agni approached It. It asked him, “Who art thou?” He replied, “I am Agni or I am Jataveda”.

verses.sa: तस्मिंस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमित्यपीदं सर्वं दहेयं यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥
verses.iast: tasmiṃstvayi kiṃ vīryamityapīdaṃ sarvaṃ daheyaṃ yadidaṃ pṛthivyāmiti ॥
verses.tr: (It said:) “What is the power in thee, such as thou art?” (Agni said:) “I can burn all this that is upon the earth.”

verses.sa: तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतद्दहेति तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाक दग्धुं स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
verses.iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetaddaheti tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśāka dagdhuṃ sa tata eva nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ॥
verses.tr: For him (It) placed there a blade of grass and said: “Burn this”. (Agni) went near it in all haste, but he could not burn it. He returned from there (and said:) “I am unable to understand who that Yaksha is”.

verses.sa: अथ वायुमब्रुवन् वायवेतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति ॥
verses.iast: atha vāyumabruvan vāyavetadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti ॥
verses.tr: Then (the gods) said to Vayu: “O Vayu, know thou this as to who this Yaksha is”. (He said:) “So be it”.

verses.sa: तदभ्यद्रवत् तमभ्यवदत् कोऽसीति वायुर्वा अहमस्मीत्यब्रवीन्मातरिश्वा वा अहमस्मीति ॥
verses.iast: tadabhyadravat tamabhyavadat ko’sīti vāyurvā ahamasmītyabravīnmātariśvā vā ahamasmīti ॥
verses.tr: Vayu approached It. It said to him, “Who art thou?” He replied, “I am Vayu or I am Matarsiva”.

verses.sa: तस्मिंस्त्वयि किं वीर्यमित्यपीदं सर्वमाददीय यदिदं पृथिव्यामिति ॥
verses.iast: tasmiṃstvayi kiṃ vīryamityapīdaṃ sarvamādadīya yadidaṃ pṛthivyāmiti ॥
verses.tr: (It said:) “What is the power in thee, such as thou art?” (Vayu said:) “I can take hold of all this that is upon the earth”.

verses.sa: तस्मै तृणं निदधावेतदादत्स्वेति तदुपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन्न शशाकादातुं स तत एव निववृते नैतदशकं विज्ञातुं यदेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
verses.iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāvetadādatsveti tadupapreyāya sarvajavena tanna śaśākādātuṃ sa tata eva nivavṛte naitadaśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yadetadyakṣamiti ॥
verses.tr: For him (It) placed there a blade of grass and said: “Take this up”. (Vayu) went near it in all haste, but he could not take it up. He returned from there (and said:) “I am unable to understand who that Yaksha is”.

verses.sa: अथेन्द्रमब्रुवन् मघवन्नेतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति तदभ्यद्रवत् तस्मात्तिरोदधे ॥
verses.iast: athendramabruvan maghavannetadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti tadabhyadravat tasmāttirodadhe ॥
verses.tr: Then (the gods) said to Indra: “O Maghava, know thou this as to who this Yaksha is”. (He said:) “So be it”. He approached It, but It disappeared from him.

verses.sa: स तस्मिन्नेवाकाशे स्त्रियमाजगाम बहुशोभमानामुमां हैमवतीं तां होवाच किमेतद्यक्षमिति ॥
verses.iast: sa tasminnevākāśe striyamājagāma bahuśobhamānāmumāṃ haimavatīṃ tāṃ hovāca kimetadyakṣamiti ॥
verses.tr: In that space itself (where the Yaksha had disappeared) Indra approached an exceedingly charming woman. To that Uma decked in gold (or to the daughter of the Himalayas), he said: “Who is this Yaksha?”

verses.sa: सा ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद्विजये महीयध्वमिति ततो हैव विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥
verses.iast: sā brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etadvijaye mahīyadhvamiti tato haiva vidāṃcakāra brahmeti ॥
verses.tr: She said: “It was Brahman. In the victory that was Brahman’s you were reveling in joy”. Then alone did Indra know for certain that It was Brahman.

verses.sa: तस्माद्वा एते देवा अतितरामिवान्यान् देवान् यदग्निर्वायुरिन्द्रस्ते ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्शुस्ते ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥
verses.iast: tasmādvā ete devā atitarāmivānyān devān yadagnirvāyurindraste hyenannediṣṭhaṃ pasparśuste hyenatprathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, these gods viz. Agni, Vayu and Indra excelled other gods, for they touched Brahman who stood very close and indeed knew first that It was Brahman.

verses.sa: तस्माद्वा इन्द्रोऽतितरामिवान्यान्देवान् स ह्येनन्नेदिष्ठं पस्पर्श स ह्येनत् प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति ॥
verses.iast: tasmādvā indro’titarāmivānyāndevān sa hyenannediṣṭhaṃ pasparśa sa hyenat prathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti ॥
verses.tr: Therefore is Indra more excellent than the other gods, for he touched Brahman who stood very close and indeed knew first that It was Brahman.

verses.sa: तस्यैष आदेशो यदेतद्विद्युतो व्यद्युतदा३ इतीन्न्यमीमिषदा३ इत्यधिदैवतम् ॥
verses.iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yadetadvidyuto vyadyutadā3 itīnnyamīmiṣadā3 ityadhidaivatam ॥
verses.tr: Its instruction (regarding meditation) is this. It is similar to that which is like a flash of lightning or like the winkling of the eye. This is (the analogy of Brahman) in the divine aspect.

verses.sa: अथाध्यात्मं यदेतद्गच्छतीव च मनोऽनेन चैतदुपस्मरत्यभीक्ष्णं संकल्पः ॥
verses.iast: athādhyātmaṃ yadetadgacchatīva ca mano’nena caitadupasmaratyabhīkṣṇaṃ saṃkalpaḥ ॥
verses.tr: Then (follows) the instruction through analogy on the aspect of the individual self. (It is wellknown that) the mind seems to attain to It, that It is continually remembered by the mind, and that the mind possesses the thought (regarding It).

verses.sa: तद्ध तद्वनं नाम तद्वनमित्युपासितव्यं स य एतदेवं वेदाभि हैनं सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाञ्छन्ति ॥
verses.iast: taddha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanamityupāsitavyaṃ sa ya etadevaṃ vedābhi hainaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāñchanti ॥
verses.tr: That Brahman is known indeed as Tadvana (worshipful or adorable to all beings); That is to be worshiped as Tadvana. To him who knows It thus verily all beings pray.

verses.sa: उपनिषदं भो ब्रूहीत्युक्ता त उपनिषद् ब्राह्मीं वाव त उपनिषदमब्रूमेति ॥
verses.iast: upaniṣadaṃ bho brūhītyuktā ta upaniṣad brāhmīṃ vāva ta upaniṣadamabrūmeti ॥
verses.tr: (Disciple:) “Revered sir, speak Upanishad to me.” (Teacher:) “I have spoken Upanishad to thee. Of Brahman verily is the Upanishad that I have spoken.”

verses.sa: तस्यै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदाः सर्वाङ्गानि सत्यमायतनम् ॥
verses.iast: tasyai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedāḥ sarvāṅgāni satyamāyatanam ॥
verses.tr: Of this knowledge austerity, self-restraint and action are the feet, the Vedas are all limbs and truth is the abode.

verses.sa: यो वा एतामेवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानमनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति प्रतितिष्ठति ॥
verses.iast: yo vā etāmevaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānamanante svarge loke jyeye pratitiṣṭhati pratitiṣṭhati ॥
verses.tr: He who knows this thus, with his sins destroyed, becomes firmly seated in the infinite, blissful and supreme Brahman. He becomes firmly seated (in Brahman).

verses.sa: ॐ इत्येतदक्षरमिदं सर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानं भूतं भवद् भविष्यदिति सर्वमोङ्कार एव यच्चान्यत् त्रिकालातीतं तदप्योङ्कार एव ॥ १॥
verses.iast: oṃ ityetadakṣaramidaṃ sarvaṃ tasyopavyākhyānaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyaditi sarvamoṅkāra eva yaccānyat trikālātītaṃ tadapyoṅkāra eva ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: All this is the letter Om. A vivid explanation of this (is begun). All that is past, present, and future is but Om. Whatever transcends the three periods of time, too, is Om.

verses.sa: सर्वं ह्येतद् ब्रह्मायमात्मा ब्रह्म सोऽयमात्मा चतुष्पात् ॥ २॥
verses.iast: sarvaṃ hyetad brahmāyamātmā brahma so’yamātmā catuṣpāt ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: All this is certainly Brahman. This Self is Brahman. This Self, as such, is possessed of four quarters.

verses.sa: जागरितस्थानो बहिष्प्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः प्रथमः पादः ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: jāgaritasthāno bahiṣprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ sthūlabhugvaiśvānaraḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: (The Self) seated in the waking state and called Vaisvanara who, possessed of the consciousness of the exterior, and seven limbs and nineteen mouths, enjoys the gross objects, is the first quarter.

verses.sa: स्वप्नस्थानोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसो द्वितीयः पादः ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: svapnasthāno’ntaḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṃśatimukhaḥ praviviktabhuktaijaso dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: (The Self) seated in the state of dream and called Taijasa who, possessed of the consciousness of the interior, and seven limbs and nineteen mouths, enjoys the subtle objects, is the second quarter.

verses.sa: यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति तत् सुषुप्तम् । सुषुप्तस्थान एकीभूतः प्रज्ञानघन एवानन्दमयो ह्यानन्दभुक् चेतोमुखः प्राज्ञस्तृतीयः पादः ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṃ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṃ paśyati tat suṣuptam । suṣuptasthāna ekībhūtaḥ prajñānaghana evānandamayo hyānandabhuk cetomukhaḥ prājñastṛtīyaḥ pādaḥ ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: Where the sleeper desires not a thing of enjoyment and sees not any dream, that state is deep sleep. (The Self) seated in the state of deep sleep and called Prajna, in whom everything is unified, who is dense with consciousness, who is full of bliss, who is certainly the enjoyer of bliss, and who is the door to the knowledge (of the preceding two states), is the third quarter.

verses.sa: एष सर्वेश्वरः एष सर्वज्ञ एषोऽन्तर्याम्येष योनिः सर्वस्य प्रभवाप्ययौ हि भूतानाम् ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: eṣa sarveśvaraḥ eṣa sarvajña eṣo’ntaryāmyeṣa yoniḥ sarvasya prabhavāpyayau hi bhūtānām ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: This is the Lord of all; this is omniscient; this is the in-dwelling controller (of all); this is the source and indeed the origin and dissolution of all beings.

verses.sa: नान्तःप्रज्ञं न बहिष्प्रज्ञं नोभयतःप्रज्ञं न प्रज्ञानघनं न प्रज्ञं नाप्रज्ञम् । अदृष्टमव्यवहार्यमग्राह्यमलक्षणं अचिन्त्यमव्यपदेश्यमेकात्मप्रत्ययसारं प्रपञ्चोपशमं शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं चतुर्थं मन्यन्ते स आत्मा स विज्ञेयः ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: nāntaḥprajñaṃ na bahiṣprajñaṃ nobhayataḥprajñaṃ na prajñānaghanaṃ na prajñaṃ nāprajñam । adṛṣṭamavyavahāryamagrāhyamalakṣaṇaṃ acintyamavyapadeśyamekātmapratyayasāraṃ prapañcopaśamaṃ śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ caturthaṃ manyante sa ātmā sa vijñeyaḥ ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: The Fourth is thought of as that which is not conscious of the internal world, nor conscious of the external world, nor conscious of both the worlds, nor dense with consciousness, nor simple consciousness, nor unconsciousness, which is unseen, actionless, incomprehensible, uninferable, unthinkable, indescribable, whose proof consists in the identity of the Self (in all states), in which all phenomena come to a cessation, and which is unchanging, auspicious, and non-dual. That is the Self; that is to be known.

verses.sa: सोऽयमात्माध्यक्षरमोङ्कारोऽधिमात्रं पादा मात्रा मात्राश्च पादा अकार उकारो मकार इति ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: so’yamātmādhyakṣaramoṅkāro’dhimātraṃ pādā mātrā mātrāśca pādā akāra ukāro makāra iti ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: That same Self, from the point of view of the syllable, is Om, and viewed from the stand point of the letters, the quarters are the letters, and the letters are the quarters. The letters are a, u and m.

verses.sa: जागरितस्थानो वैश्वानरोऽकारः प्रथमा मात्राऽऽप्तेरादिमत्त्वाद् वाऽऽप्नोति ह वै सर्वान् कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: jāgaritasthāno vaiśvānaro’kāraḥ prathamā mātrā’’pterādimattvād vā’’pnoti ha vai sarvān kāmānādiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: Vaisvanara seated in the waking state is the first letter a, owing to its all-pervasiveness or being the first. He who knows thus verily accomplishes all longings and becomes the first.

verses.sa: स्वप्नस्थानस्तैजस उकारो द्वितीया मात्रोत्कर्षात् उभयत्वाद्वोत्कर्षति ह वै ज्ञानसन्ततिं समानश्च भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति य एवं वेद ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: svapnasthānastaijasa ukāro dvitīyā mātrotkarṣāt ubhayatvādvotkarṣati ha vai jñānasantatiṃ samānaśca bhavati nāsyābrahmavitkule bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: Taijasa seated in the dream is u, the second letter (of Om), owing to the similarity of excellence or intermediate position. He who knows thus verily advances the bounds of his knowledge and becomes equal (to all) and none who is not a knower of Brahman is born in his family.

verses.sa: सुषुप्तस्थानः प्राज्ञो मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा मितेरपीतेर्वा मिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: suṣuptasthānaḥ prājño makārastṛtīyā mātrā miterapītervā minoti ha vā idaṃ sarvamapītiśca bhavati ya evaṃ veda ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: Prajna seated in the state of deep sleep is m, the third letter (of Om), because of his being the measure or the entity wherein all become absorbed. He who knows thus measures all this and absorbs all.

verses.sa: अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः प्रपञ्चोपशमः शिवोऽद्वैत एवमोङ्कार आत्मैव संविशत्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥ १२॥
verses.iast: amātraścaturtho’vyavahāryaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivo’dvaita evamoṅkāra ātmaiva saṃviśatyātmanā’’tmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥ 12॥
verses.tr: That which is without letters (parts) is the Fourth, beyond apprehension through ordinary means, the cessation of the phenomenal world, the auspicious and the non-dual. Thus Om is certainly the Self. He who knows thus enters the Self by the Self.

verses.sa: ॐ ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमः संबभूव विश्वस्य कर्ता भुवनस्य गोप्ता । स ब्रह्मविद्यां सर्वविद्याप्रतिष्ठामथर्वाय ज्येष्ठपुत्राय प्राह ॥ १॥
verses.iast: oṃ brahmā devānāṃ prathamaḥ saṃbabhūva viśvasya kartā bhuvanasya goptā । sa brahmavidyāṃ sarvavidyāpratiṣṭhāmatharvāya jyeṣṭhaputrāya prāha ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: Om ! Brahma, the creator of the Universe and the protector of the world, was the first among the gods to manifest Himself. To His eldest son Atharva He imparted that knowledge of Brahman that is the basis of all knowledge.

verses.sa: अथर्वणे यां प्रवदेत ब्रह्माऽथर्वा तं पुरोवाचाङ्गिरे ब्रह्मविद्याम् । स भारद्वाजाय सत्यवाहाय प्राह भारद्वाजोऽङ्गिरसे परावराम् ॥ २॥
verses.iast: atharvaṇe yāṃ pravadeta brahmā’tharvā taṃ purovācāṅgire brahmavidyām । sa bhāradvājāya satyavāhāya prāha bhāradvājo’ṅgirase parāvarām ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: The Knowledge of Brahman that Brahma imparted to Atharva, Atharva transmitted to Angir in days of yore. He (Angir) passed it on to Satyavaha of the line of Bharadvaja. He of the line of Bharadvaja handed down to Angiras this knowledge that had been received in succession from the higher by the lower ones.

verses.sa: शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: śaunako ha vai mahāśālo’ṅgirasaṃ vidhivadupasannaḥ papraccha । kasminnu bhagavo vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: Saunaka, well known as a great householder, having approached Angiras duly, asked, ‘O adorable sir, (which is that thing) which having been known, all this becomes known ?’

verses.sa: तस्मै स होवाच । द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये इति ह स्म यद्ब्रह्मविदो वदन्ति परा चैवापरा च ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: tasmai sa hovāca । dve vidye veditavye iti ha sma yadbrahmavido vadanti parā caivāparā ca ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: To him he said, ‘"There are two kinds of knowledge to be acquired – the higher and the lower"; this is what, as tradition runs, the knowers of the import of the Vedas say.’

verses.sa: तत्रापरा ऋग्वेदो यजुर्वेदः सामवेदोऽथर्ववेदः शिक्षा कल्पो व्याकरणं निरुक्तं छन्दो ज्योतिषमिति । अथ परा यया तदक्षरमधिगम्यते ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: tatrāparā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo’tharvavedaḥ śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chando jyotiṣamiti । atha parā yayā tadakṣaramadhigamyate ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: Of these, the lower comprises the Rig-Veda, Yajur-Veda, Sama-Veda, Atharva-Veda, the science of pronunciation etc., the code of rituals, grammar, etymology, metre and astrology. Then there is the higher (knowledge) by which is attained that Imperishable.

verses.sa: यत्तदद्रेश्यमग्राह्यमगोत्रमवर्णमचक्षुःश्रोत्रं तदपाणिपादम् । नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं तदव्ययं यद्भूतयोनिं परिपश्यन्ति धीराः ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: yattadadreśyamagrāhyamagotramavarṇamacakṣuḥśrotraṃ tadapāṇipādam । nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ tadavyayaṃ yadbhūtayoniṃ paripaśyanti dhīrāḥ ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: (By the higher knowledge) the wise realize everywhere that which cannot be perceived and grasped, which is without source, features, eyes, and ears, which has neither hands nor feet, which is eternal, multiformed, all-pervasive, extremely subtle, and undiminishing and which is the source of all.

verses.sa: यथोर्णनाभिः सृजते गृह्णते च यथा पृथिव्यामोषधयः संभवन्ति । यथा सतः पुरुषात्केशलोमानि तथाऽक्षरात्संभवतीह विश्वम् ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: yathorṇanābhiḥ sṛjate gṛhṇate ca yathā pṛthivyāmoṣadhayaḥ saṃbhavanti । yathā sataḥ puruṣātkeśalomāni tathā’kṣarātsaṃbhavatīha viśvam ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: As a spider spreads out and withdraws (its thread), as on the earth grow the herbs (and trees), and as from a living man issues out hair (on the head and body), so out of the Imperishable does the Universe emerge here (in this phenomenal creation).

verses.sa: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते । अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम् ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: tapasā cīyate brahma tato’nnamabhijāyate । annātprāṇo manaḥ satyaṃ lokāḥ karmasu cāmṛtam ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: Through knowledge Brahman increases in size. From that is born food (the Unmanifested). From food evolves Prana (Hiranyagarbha); (thence the cosmic) mind; (thence) the five elements; (thence) the worlds; (thence) the immortality that is in karmas.

verses.sa: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्य ज्ञानमयं तपः । तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपमन्नं च जायते ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavidyasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ । tasmādetadbrahma nāma rūpamannaṃ ca jāyate ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: From Him, who is omniscient in general and all-knowing in detail and whose austerity is constituted by knowledge, evolve this (derivative) Brahman, name, colour and food.

verses.sa: तदेतत्सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा संततानि । तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके ॥ १॥
verses.iast: tadetatsatyaṃ mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayo yānyapaśyaṃstāni tretāyāṃ bahudhā saṃtatāni । tānyācaratha niyataṃ satyakāmā eṣa vaḥ panthāḥ sukṛtasya loke ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: That thing that is such, is true. The karmas that the wise discovered in the mantras are accomplished variously (in the context of the sacrifice) where the three Vedic duties get united. You perform them for ever with desire for the true results. This is your path leading to the fruits of karma acquired by yourselves.

verses.sa: यदा लेलायते ह्यर्चिः समिद्धे हव्यवाहने । तदाऽऽज्यभागावन्तरेणाऽऽहुतीः प्रतिपादयेच्छ्रद्धया हुतम् ॥ २॥
verses.iast: yadā lelāyate hyarciḥ samiddhe havyavāhane । tadā’’jyabhāgāvantareṇā’’hutīḥ pratipādayecchraddhayā hutam ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: When, the fire being set ablaze, the flame shoots up, one should offer the oblations into that part that is in between the right and the left.

verses.sa: यस्याग्निहोत्रमदर्शमपौर्णमासमचातुर्मास्यमनाग्रयणमतिथिवर्जितं च । अहुतमवैश्वदेवमविधिना हुतमासप्तमांस्तस्य लोकान् हिनस्ति ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: yasyāgnihotramadarśamapaurṇamāsamacāturmāsyamanāgrayaṇamatithivarjitaṃ ca । ahutamavaiśvadevamavidhinā hutamāsaptamāṃstasya lokān hinasti ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: It (i.e. the Agnihotra) destroys the seven worlds of that man whose Agnihotra (sacrifice) is without Darsa and Paurnamasa (rites), devoid of Chaturmasya, bereft of Agrayana, unblest with guests, goes unperformed, is unaccompanied by Vaisvadeva (rite) and is performed perfunctorily.

verses.sa: काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा । स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā । sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: Kali, Karali, Manojava and Sulohita and that which is Sudhumravarna, as also Sphulingini, and the shining Visvaruchi – these are the seven flaming tongues.

verses.sa: एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं चाहुतयो ह्याददायन् । तं नयन्त्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: eteṣu yaścarate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālaṃ cāhutayo hyādadāyan । taṃ nayantyetāḥ sūryasya raśmayo yatra devānāṃ patireko’dhivāsaḥ ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: These oblations turn into the rays of the sun and taking him up they lead him, who performs the rites in these shining flames at the proper time, to where the single lord of the gods presides over all.

verses.sa: एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहन्ति । प्रियां वाचमभिवदन्त्योऽर्चयन्त्य एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: ehyehīti tamāhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ sūryasya raśmibhiryajamānaṃ vahanti । priyāṃ vācamabhivadantyo’rcayantya eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmalokaḥ ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: Saying, ‘Come, come’, uttering pleasing words such as, ‘This is your well-earned, virtuous path which leads to heaven’, and offering him adoration, the scintillating oblations carry the sacrificer along the rays of the sun.

verses.sa: प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपा अष्टादशोक्तमवरं येषु कर्म । एतच्छ्रेयो येऽभिनन्दन्ति मूढा जरामृत्युं ते पुनरेवापि यन्ति ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: plavā hyete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktamavaraṃ yeṣu karma । etacchreyo ye’bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punarevāpi yanti ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: Since these eighteen constituents of a sacrifice, on whom the inferior karma has been said to rest, are perishable because of their fragility, therefore those ignorant people who get elated with the idea ‘This is (the cause of) bliss’, undergo old age and death over again.

verses.sa: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः । जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: avidyāyāmantare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃmanyamānāḥ । jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: Remaining within the fold of ignorance and thinking, ‘We are ourselves wise and learned’, the fools, while being buffeted very much, ramble about like the blind led by the blind alone.

verses.sa: अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमाना वयं कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यन्ति बालाः । यत्कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयन्ति रागात्तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्च्यवन्ते ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: avidyāyāṃ bahudhā vartamānā vayaṃ kṛtārthā ityabhimanyanti bālāḥ । yatkarmiṇo na pravedayanti rāgāttenāturāḥ kṣīṇalokāścyavante ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: Continuing diversely in the midst of ignorance, the unenlightened take airs by thinking, ‘We have attained the goal.’ Since the men, engaged in karma, do not understand (the truth) under the influence of attachment, thereby they become afflicted with sorrow and are deprived of heaven on the exhaustion of the results of karma.

verses.sa: इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः । नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं लोकं हीनतरं वा विशन्ति ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: iṣṭāpūrtaṃ manyamānā variṣṭhaṃ nānyacchreyo vedayante pramūḍhāḥ । nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte’nubhūtvemaṃ lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśanti ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: The deluded fools, believing the rites inculcated by the Vedas and the Smritis to be the highest, do not understand the other thing (that leads to) liberation. They, having enjoyed (the fruits of actions) in the abode of pleasure on the heights of heaven, enter this world or an inferior one.

verses.sa: तपःश्रद्धे ये ह्युपवसन्त्यरण्ये शान्ता विद्वांसो भैक्ष्यचर्यां चरन्तः । सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: tapaḥśraddhe ye hyupavasantyaraṇye śāntā vidvāṃso bhaikṣyacaryāṃ carantaḥ । sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti yatrāmṛtaḥ sa puruṣo hyavyayātmā ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: Those who live in the forest, while begging for alms – viz. those (forest-dwellers and hermits) who resort to the duties of their respective stages of life as well as to meditation – and the learned (householders) who have their senses under control – (they) after becoming freed from dirt, go by the path of the sun to where lives that Purusha, immortal and undecaying by nature.

verses.sa: परीक्ष्य लोकान् कर्मचितान् ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन । तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत् समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम् ॥ १२॥
verses.iast: parīkṣya lokān karmacitān brāhmaṇo nirvedamāyānnāstyakṛtaḥ kṛtena । tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurumevābhigacchet samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham ॥ 12॥
verses.tr: A Brahmana should resort to renunciation after examining the worlds acquired through karma, with the help of this maxim: ‘There is nothing (here) that is not the result of karma; so what is the need of (performing) karma ?’ For knowing that Reality he should go, with sacrificial faggots in hand, only to a teacher versed in the Vedas and absorbed in Brahman.

verses.sa: तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय सम्यक् प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय । येनाक्षरं पुरुषं वेद सत्यं प्रोवाच तां तत्त्वतो ब्रह्मविद्याम् ॥ १३॥
verses.iast: tasmai sa vidvānupasannāya samyak praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya । yenākṣaraṃ puruṣaṃ veda satyaṃ provāca tāṃ tattvato brahmavidyām ॥ 13॥
verses.tr: To him who has approached duly, whose heart is calm and whose outer organs are under control, that man of enlightenment should adequately impart that knowledge of Brahman by which one realizes the true and imperishable Purusha.

verses.sa: तदेतत्सत्यं यथा सुदीप्तात्पावकाद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः । तथाऽक्षराद्विविधाः सोम्य भावाः प्रजायन्ते तत्र चैवापियन्ति ॥ १॥
verses.iast: tadetatsatyaṃ yathā sudīptātpāvakādvisphuliṅgāḥ sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ । tathā’kṣarādvividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ prajāyante tatra caivāpiyanti ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: That thing that is such, is true. As from a fire fully ablaze, fly off sparks in their thousands that are akin to the fire, similarly O goodlooking one, from the Imperishable originate different kinds of creatures and into It again they merge.

verses.sa: दिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः पुरुषः सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजः । अप्राणो ह्यमनाः शुभ्रो ह्यक्षरात्परतः परः ॥ २॥
verses.iast: divyo hyamūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sabāhyābhyantaro hyajaḥ । aprāṇo hyamanāḥ śubhro hyakṣarātparataḥ paraḥ ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: The Purusha is transcendental, since He is formless. And since He is coextensive with all that is external and internal and since He is birthless, therefore He is without vital force and without mind; He is pure and superior to the (other) superior imperishable (Maya).

verses.sa: एतस्माज्जायते प्राणो मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च । खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: etasmājjāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca । khaṃ vāyurjyotirāpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: From Him originates the vital force as well as the mind, all the senses, space, air, fire, water, and earth that supports everything.

verses.sa: अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग्विवृताश्च वेदाः । वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: agnirmūrdhā cakṣuṣī candrasūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāgvivṛtāśca vedāḥ । vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvamasya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hyeṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: The indwelling Self of all is surely He of whom the heaven is the head, the moon and sun are the two eyes, the directions are the two ears, the revealed Vedas are the speech, air is the vital force, the whole Universe is the heart, and (It is He) from whose two feet emerged the earth.

verses.sa: तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः सोमात्पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्याम् । पुमान् रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायां बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात्संप्रसूताः ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: tasmādagniḥ samidho yasya sūryaḥ somātparjanya oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām । pumān retaḥ siñcati yoṣitāyāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣātsaṃprasūtāḥ ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: From Him emerges the fire (i.e. heaven) of which the fuel is the sun. From the moon emerges cloud, and (from cloud) the herbs and corns on the earth. A man sheds the semen into a woman. From the Purusha have originated many creatures.

verses.sa: तस्मादृचः साम यजूꣳषि दीक्षा यज्ञाश्च सर्वे क्रतवो दक्षिणाश्च । संवत्सरश्च यजमानश्च लोकाः सोमो यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: tasmādṛcaḥ sāma yajūꣳṣi dīkṣā yajñāśca sarve kratavo dakṣiṇāśca । saṃvatsaraśca yajamānaśca lokāḥ somo yatra pavate yatra sūryaḥ ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: From Him (emerge) the Rik, Sama and Yajur mantras, initiation, all the sacrifices – whether with or without the sacrificial stake – offerings to Brahmanas, the year, the sacrificer, and the worlds where the moon sacrifices (all) and where the sun (shines).

verses.sa: तस्माच्च देवा बहुधा संप्रसूताः साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयाꣳसि । प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च श्रद्धा सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: tasmācca devā bahudhā saṃprasūtāḥ sādhyā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāꣳsi । prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaśca śraddhā satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidhiśca ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: And from Him duly emerged the gods in various groups, the Sadhyas, human beings, beasts, birds, life, rice and barley, as well as austerity, faith, truth, continence and dutifulness.

verses.sa: सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मात्सप्तार्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः । सप्त इमे लोका येषु चरन्ति प्राणा गुहाशया निहिताः सप्त सप्त ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmātsaptārciṣaḥ samidhaḥ sapta homāḥ । sapta ime lokā yeṣu caranti prāṇā guhāśayā nihitāḥ sapta sapta ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: From Him emerge the seven sense-organs, the seven flames, the seven kinds of fuel, the seven oblations, and these seven seats where move the sense-organs that sleep in the cavity, (and) have been deposited (by God) in groups of seven.

verses.sa: अतः समुद्रा गिरयश्च सर्वेऽस्मात्स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्वरूपाः । अतश्च सर्वा ओषधयो रसश्च येनैष भूतैस्तिष्ठते ह्यन्तरात्मा ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: ataḥ samudrā girayaśca sarve’smātsyandante sindhavaḥ sarvarūpāḥ । ataśca sarvā oṣadhayo rasaśca yenaiṣa bhūtaistiṣṭhate hyantarātmā ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: From Him emerge all the oceans and all the mountains. From Him flow out the rivers of various forms. And from Him issue all the corns as well as the juice, by virtue of which the internal self verily exists in the midst of the elements.

verses.sa: पुरुष एवेदं विश्वं कर्म तपो ब्रह्म परामृतम् । एतद्यो वेद निहितं गुहायां सोऽविद्याग्रन्थिं विकिरतीह सोम्य ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam । etadyo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ so’vidyāgranthiṃ vikiratīha somya ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: The Purusha alone is all this – (comprising) karma and knowledge. He who knows this supreme, immortal Brahman, existing in the heart, destroys here the knot of ignorance, O good-looking one !

verses.sa: आविः संनिहितं गुहाचरं नाम महत्पदमत्रैतत्समर्पितम् । एजत्प्राणन्निमिषच्च यदेतज्जानथ सदसद्वरेण्यं परं विज्ञानाद्यद्वरिष्ठं प्रजानाम् ॥ १॥
verses.iast: āviḥ saṃnihitaṃ guhācaraṃ nāma mahatpadamatraitatsamarpitam । ejatprāṇannimiṣacca yadetajjānatha sadasadvareṇyaṃ paraṃ vijñānādyadvariṣṭhaṃ prajānām ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: (It is) effulgent, near at hand, and well known as moving in the heart, and (It is) the great goal. On It are fixed all these that move, breathe, and wink or do not wink. Know this One which comprises the gross and the subtle, which is beyond the ordinary knowledge of creatures, and which is the most desirable and the highest of all.

verses.sa: यदर्चिमद्यदणुभ्योऽणु च यस्मिँल्लोका निहिता लोकिनश्च । तदेतदक्षरं ब्रह्म स प्राणस्तदु वाङ्मनः तदेतत्सत्यं तदमृतं तद्वेद्धव्यं सोम्य विद्धि ॥ २॥
verses.iast: yadarcimadyadaṇubhyo’ṇu ca yasmim̐llokā nihitā lokinaśca । tadetadakṣaraṃ brahma sa prāṇastadu vāṅmanaḥ tadetatsatyaṃ tadamṛtaṃ tadveddhavyaṃ somya viddhi ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: That which is bright and is subtler than the subtle, and that on which are fixed all the worlds as well as the dwellers of the worlds, is this immutable Brahman; It is this vital force; It, again, is speech and mind. This Entity, that is such, is true. It is immortal. It is to be penetrated, O good-looking one, shoot (at It).

verses.sa: धनुर्गृहीत्वौपनिषदं महास्त्रं शरं ह्युपासानिशितं संधयीत । आयम्य तद्भावगतेन चेतसा लक्ष्यं तदेवाक्षरं सोम्य विद्धि ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: dhanurgṛhītvaupaniṣadaṃ mahāstraṃ śaraṃ hyupāsāniśitaṃ saṃdhayīta । āyamya tadbhāvagatena cetasā lakṣyaṃ tadevākṣaraṃ somya viddhi ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: Taking hold of the bow, the great weapon familiar in the Upanishads, one should fix on it an arrow sharpened with meditation. Drawing the string, O good-looking one, hit that very target that is the Imperishable, with the mind absorbed in Its thought.

verses.sa: प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्यात्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते । अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत् ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hyātmā brahma tallakṣyamucyate । apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravattanmayo bhavet ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: Om is the bow; the soul is the arrow; and Brahman is called its target. It is to be hit by an unerring man. One should become one with It just like an arrow.

verses.sa: यस्मिन् द्यौः पृथिवी चान्तरिक्षमोतं मनः सह प्राणैश्च सर्वैः । तमेवैकं जानथ आत्मानमन्या वाचो विमुञ्चथामृतस्यैष सेतुः ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: yasmin dyauḥ pṛthivī cāntarikṣamotaṃ manaḥ saha prāṇaiśca sarvaiḥ । tamevaikaṃ jānatha ātmānamanyā vāco vimuñcathāmṛtasyaiṣa setuḥ ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: Know that Self alone that is one without a second, on which are strung heaven, the earth and the inter-space, the mind and the vital forces together with all the other organs; and give up all other talks. This is the bridge leading to immortality.

verses.sa: अरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः । स एषोऽन्तश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः । ओमित्येवं ध्यायथ आत्मानं स्वस्ति वः पाराय तमसः परस्तात् ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: arā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ । sa eṣo’ntaścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ । omityevaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānaṃ svasti vaḥ pārāya tamasaḥ parastāt ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: Within that (heart) in which are fixed the nerves like the spokes on the hub of a chariot wheel, moves this aforesaid Self by becoming multiformed. Meditate on the Self thus with the help of Om. May you be free from hindrances in going to the other shore beyond darkness.

verses.sa: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्वविद्यस्यैष महिमा भुवि । दिव्ये ब्रह्मपुरे ह्येष व्योम्न्यात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ मनोमयः प्राणशरीरनेता प्रतिष्ठितोऽन्ने हृदयं संनिधाय । तद्विज्ञानेन परिपश्यन्ति धीरा आनन्दरूपममृतं यद्विभाति ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavidyasyaiṣa mahimā bhuvi । divye brahmapure hyeṣa vyomnyātmā pratiṣṭhitaḥ ॥ manomayaḥ prāṇaśarīranetā pratiṣṭhito’nne hṛdayaṃ saṃnidhāya । tadvijñānena paripaśyanti dhīrā ānandarūpamamṛtaṃ yadvibhāti ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: That Self which is omniscient in general and all-knowing in detail and which has such glory in this world – that Self, which is of this kind – is seated in the space within the luminous city of Brahman. It is conditioned by the mind, It is the carrier of the vital forces and the body, It is seated in food by placing the intellect (in the cavity of the heart). Through their knowledge, the discriminating people realize that Self as existing in Its fullness everywhere – the Self that shines surpassingly as blissfulness and immortality.

verses.sa: भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: bhidyate hṛdayagranthiśchidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ । kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: When that Self, which is both the high and the low, is realized, the knot of the heart gets united, all doubts become solved, and all one’s actions become dissipated.

verses.sa: हिरण्मये परे कोशे विरजं ब्रह्म निष्कलम् । तच्छुभ्रं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिस्तद्यदात्मविदो विदुः ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: hiraṇmaye pare kośe virajaṃ brahma niṣkalam । tacchubhraṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotistadyadātmavido viduḥ ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: In the supreme, bright sheath is Brahman, free from taints and without parts. It is pure, and is the Light of lights. It is that which the knowers of the Self realize.

verses.sa: न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto’yamagniḥ । tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon or the stars; nor do these flashes of lightning shine there. How can this fire do so ? Everything shines according as He does so; by His light all this shines diversely.

verses.sa: ब्रह्मैवेदममृतं पुरस्ताद्ब्रह्म पश्चाद्ब्रह्म दक्षिणतश्चोत्तरेण । अधश्चोर्ध्वं च प्रसृतं ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमिदं वरिष्ठम् ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: brahmaivedamamṛtaṃ purastādbrahma paścādbrahma dakṣiṇataścottareṇa । adhaścordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaṃ brahmaivedaṃ viśvamidaṃ variṣṭham ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: All this that is in front is but Brahman, the immortal. Brahman is at the back, as also on the right and the left. It is extended above and below, too. This world is nothing but Brahman, the highest.

verses.sa: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति ॥ १॥
verses.iast: dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pariṣasvajāte । tayoranyaḥ pippalaṃ svādvattyanaśnannanyo abhicākaśīti ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: Two birds that are ever associated and have similar names, cling to the same tree. Of these, one eats the fruit of divergent tastes, and the other looks on without eating.

verses.sa: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥ २॥
verses.iast: samāne vṛkṣe puruṣo nimagno’nīśayā śocati muhyamānaḥ । juṣṭaṃ yadā paśyatyanyamīśamasya mahimānamiti vītaśokaḥ ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: On the same tree, the individual soul remains drowned (i.e. stuck), as it were; and so it moans, being worried by its impotence. When it sees thus the other, the adored Lord, and His glory, then it becomes liberated from sorrow.

verses.sa: यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम् । तदा विद्वान् पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: yadā paśyaḥ paśyate rukmavarṇaṃ kartāramīśaṃ puruṣaṃ brahmayonim । tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyamupaiti ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: When the seer sees the Purusha – the golden-hued, creator, lord, and the source of the inferior Brahman – then the illumined one completely shakes off both merit and demerit, becomes taintless, and attains absolute equality.

verses.sa: प्राणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन् विद्वान् भवते नातिवादी । आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: prāṇo hyeṣa yaḥ sarvabhūtairvibhāti vijānan vidvān bhavate nātivādī । ātmakrīḍa ātmaratiḥ kriyāvāneṣa brahmavidāṃ variṣṭhaḥ ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: This one is verily the Vital Force which shines divergently through all beings. Knowing this, the illumined man has no (further) occasion to go beyond anything in his talk. He disports in the Self, delights in the Self, and is engrossed in (spiritual) effort. This one is the chief among the knowers of Brahman.

verses.sa: सत्येन लभ्यस्तपसा ह्येष आत्मा सम्यग्ज्ञानेन ब्रह्मचर्येण नित्यम् । अन्तःशरीरे ज्योतिर्मयो हि शुभ्रो यं पश्यन्ति यतयः क्षीणदोषाः ॥ ५॥
verses.iast: satyena labhyastapasā hyeṣa ātmā samyagjñānena brahmacaryeṇa nityam । antaḥśarīre jyotirmayo hi śubhro yaṃ paśyanti yatayaḥ kṣīṇadoṣāḥ ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: The bright and pure Self within the body, that the monks with (habitual effort and) attenuated blemishes see, is attainable verily through truth, concentration, complete knowledge, and continence, practised constantly.

verses.sa: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत्सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: satyameva jayate nānṛtaṃ satyena panthā vitato devayānaḥ । yenākramantyṛṣayo hyāptakāmā yatra tatsatyasya paramaṃ nidhānam ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: Truth alone wins, and not untruth. By truth is laid the path called Devayana, by which the desireless seers ascend to where exists the supreme treasure attainable through truth.

verses.sa: बृहच्च तद्दिव्यमचिन्त्यरूपं सूक्ष्माच्च तत्सूक्ष्मतरं विभाति । दूरात्सुदूरे तदिहान्तिके च पश्यत्स्विहैव निहितं गुहायाम् ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: bṛhacca taddivyamacintyarūpaṃ sūkṣmācca tatsūkṣmataraṃ vibhāti । dūrātsudūre tadihāntike ca paśyatsvihaiva nihitaṃ guhāyām ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: It is great and self-effulgent; and Its form is unthinkable. It is subtler than the subtle. It shines diversely. It is farther away than the far-off, and It is near at hand in this body. Among sentient beings It is (perceived as) seated in this very body, in the cavity of the heart.

verses.sa: न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा । ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्वस्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā nānyairdevaistapasā karmaṇā vā । jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattvastatastu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: It is not comprehended through the eye, nor through speech, nor through the other senses; nor is It attained through austerity or karma. Since one becomes purified in mind through the favourableness of the intellect, therefore can one see that indivisible Self through meditation.

verses.sa: एषोऽणुरात्मा चेतसा वेदितव्यो यस्मिन्प्राणः पञ्चधा संविवेश । प्राणैश्चित्तं सर्वमोतं प्रजानां यस्मिन्विशुद्धे विभवत्येष आत्मा ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: eṣo’ṇurātmā cetasā veditavyo yasminprāṇaḥ pañcadhā saṃviveśa । prāṇaiścittaṃ sarvamotaṃ prajānāṃ yasminviśuddhe vibhavatyeṣa ātmā ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: Within (the heart in) the body, where the vital force has entered in five forms, is this subtle Self to be realized through that intelligence by which is pervaded the entire mind as well as the motor and sensory organs of all creatures. And It is to be known in the mind, which having become purified, this Self reveals Itself distinctly.

verses.sa: यं यं लोकं मनसा संविभाति विशुद्धसत्त्वः कामयते यांश्च कामान् । तं तं लोकं जयते तांश्च कामांस्तस्मादात्मज्ञं ह्यर्चयेद्भूतिकामः ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: yaṃ yaṃ lokaṃ manasā saṃvibhāti viśuddhasattvaḥ kāmayate yāṃśca kāmān । taṃ taṃ lokaṃ jayate tāṃśca kāmāṃstasmādātmajñaṃ hyarcayedbhūtikāmaḥ ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: The man of pure mind wins those worlds which he mentally wishes for and those enjoyable things which he covets. Therefore one, desirous of prosperity, should adore the knower of the Self.

verses.sa: स वेदैतत्परमं ब्रह्म धाम यत्र विश्वं निहितं भाति शुभ्रम् । उपासते पुरुषं ये ह्यकामास्ते शुक्रमेतदतिवर्तन्ति धीराः ॥ १॥
verses.iast: sa vedaitatparamaṃ brahma dhāma yatra viśvaṃ nihitaṃ bhāti śubhram । upāsate puruṣaṃ ye hyakāmāste śukrametadativartanti dhīrāḥ ॥ 1॥
verses.tr: He knows this supreme abode, this Brahman, in which is placed the Universe and which shines holy. Those wise ones indeed, who having become desireless, worship this (enlightened) person, transcend this human seed.

verses.sa: कामान् यः कामयते मन्यमानः स कामभिर्जायते तत्र तत्र । पर्याप्तकामस्य कृतात्मनस्तु इहैव सर्वे प्रविलीयन्ति कामाः ॥ २॥
verses.iast: kāmān yaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ sa kāmabhirjāyate tatra tatra । paryāptakāmasya kṛtātmanastu ihaiva sarve pravilīyanti kāmāḥ ॥ 2॥
verses.tr: He who covets the desirable things, while brooding (on the virtues), is born amidst those very surroundings along with the desires. But for one who has got his wishes fulfilled and who is Selfpoised, all the longings vanish even here.

verses.sa: नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्यैष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूं स्वाम् ॥ ३॥
verses.iast: nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena । yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyastasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām ॥ 3॥
verses.tr: This Self is not attained through study, nor through the intellect, nor through much hearing. The very Self which this one (i.e. the aspirant) seeks is attainable through that fact of seeking; this Self of his reveals Its own nature.

verses.sa: नायमात्मा बलहीनेन लभ्यो न च प्रमादात्तपसो वाप्यलिङ्गात् । एतैरुपायैर्यतते यस्तु विद्वांस्तस्यैष आत्मा विशते ब्रह्मधाम ॥ ४॥
verses.iast: nāyamātmā balahīnena labhyo na ca pramādāttapaso vāpyaliṅgāt । etairupāyairyatate yastu vidvāṃstasyaiṣa ātmā viśate brahmadhāma ॥ 4॥
verses.tr: This Self is not attained by one devoid of strength, nor through delusion, nor through knowledge unassociated with monasticism. But the Self of that knower, who strives through these means, enters into the abode that is Brahman.

verses.sa: संप्राप्यैनमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशान्ताः । ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीरा युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशन्ति ॥ ५॥
