verses.iast: saṃprāpyainamṛṣayo jñānatṛptāḥ kṛtātmāno vītarāgāḥ praśāntāḥ । te sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrā yuktātmānaḥ sarvamevāviśanti ॥ 5॥
verses.tr: Having attained this, the seers become contented with their knowledge, established in the Self, freed from attachment, and composed. Having realized the all-pervasive One everywhere, these discriminating people, ever merged in contemplation, enter into the All.

verses.sa: वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः संन्यासयोगाद्यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः । ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वे ॥ ६॥
verses.iast: vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthāḥ saṃnyāsayogādyatayaḥ śuddhasattvāḥ । te brahmalokeṣu parāntakāle parāmṛtāḥ parimucyanti sarve ॥ 6॥
verses.tr: Those to whom the entity presented by the Vedantic knowledge has become fully ascertained, who are assiduous and have become pure in mind through the Yoga of monasticism – all of them, at the supreme moment of final departure, become identified with the supreme Immortality in the worlds that are Brahman, and they become freed on every side.

verses.sa: गताः कलाः पञ्चदश प्रतिष्ठा देवाश्च सर्वे प्रतिदेवतासु । कर्माणि विज्ञानमयश्च आत्मा परेऽव्यये सर्वे एकीभवन्ति ॥ ७॥
verses.iast: gatāḥ kalāḥ pañcadaśa pratiṣṭhā devāśca sarve pratidevatāsu । karmāṇi vijñānamayaśca ātmā pare’vyaye sarve ekībhavanti ॥ 7॥
verses.tr: To their sources repair the fifteen constituents (of the body) and to their respective gods go all the gods (of the senses). The karmas and the soul appearing like the intellect, all become unified with the supreme Undecaying.

verses.sa: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय । तथा विद्वान् नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ॥ ८॥
verses.iast: yathā nadyaḥ syandamānāḥ samudre’staṃ gacchanti nāmarūpe vihāya । tathā vidvān nāmarūpādvimuktaḥ parātparaṃ puruṣamupaiti divyam ॥ 8॥
verses.tr: As rivers, flowing down, become indistinguishable on reaching the sea by giving up their names and forms, so also the illumined soul, having become freed from name and form, reaches the self-effulgent Purusha that is higher than the higher (Maya).

verses.sa: स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति । तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति ॥ ९॥
verses.iast: sa yo ha vai tatparamaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati nāsyābrahmavitkule bhavati । tarati śokaṃ tarati pāpmānaṃ guhāgranthibhyo vimukto’mṛto bhavati ॥ 9॥
verses.tr: Anyone who knows that supreme Brahman becomes Brahman indeed. In his line is not born anyone who does not know Brahman. He overcomes grief, and rises above aberrations; and becoming freed from the knots of the heart, he attains immortality.

verses.sa: तदेतदृचाऽभ्युक्तम् । क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः । तेषामेवैतां ब्रह्मविद्यां वदेत शिरोव्रतं विधिवद्यैस्तु चीर्णम् ॥ १०॥
verses.iast: tadetadṛcā’bhyuktam । kriyāvantaḥ śrotriyā brahmaniṣṭhāḥ svayaṃ juhvata ekarṣiṃ śraddhayantaḥ । teṣāmevaitāṃ brahmavidyāṃ vadeta śirovrataṃ vidhivadyaistu cīrṇam ॥ 10॥
verses.tr: This (rule) has been revealed by the mantra (which runs thus): ‘To them alone should one expound this knowledge of b who are engaged in the practice of disciplines, versed in the Vedas, and indeed devoted to Brahman, who personally sacrifice to the fire called Ekarsi with faith, and by whom has been duly accomplished the vow of holding fire on the head.’

verses.sa: तदेतत्सत्यमृषिरङ्गिराः पुरोवाच नैतदचीर्णव्रतोऽधीते । नमः परमऋषिभ्यो नमः परमऋषिभ्यः ॥ ११॥
verses.iast: tadetatsatyamṛṣiraṅgirāḥ purovāca naitadacīrṇavrato’dhīte । namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyo namaḥ paramaṛṣibhyaḥ ॥ 11॥
verses.tr: The seer Angiras spoke of this Truth in the days of yore. One that has not fulfilled the vow does not read this. Salutation to the great seers. Salutation to the great seers.

verses.sa: अथ हैनं सुकेशा भारद्वाजः पप्रच्छ । भगवन् हिरण्यनाभः कौसल्यो राजपुत्रो मामुपेत्यैतं प्रश्नमपृच्छत । षोडशकलं भारद्वाज पुरुषं वेत्थ । तमहं कुमारमब्रुवं नाहमिमं वेद । यद्यहमिममवेदिषं कथं ते नावक्ष्यमिति । समूलो वा एष परिशुष्यति योऽनृतमभिवदति तस्मान्नार्हाम्यनृतं वक्तुम् । स तूष्णीं रथमारुह्य प्रवव्राज । तं त्वा पृच्छामि क्वासौ पुरुष इति ॥ ६.१॥
verses.iast: atha hainaṃ sukeśā bhāradvājaḥ papraccha । bhagavan hiraṇyanābhaḥ kausalyo rājaputro māmupetyaitaṃ praśnamapṛcchata । ṣoḍaśakalaṃ bhāradvāja puruṣaṃ vettha । tamahaṃ kumāramabruvaṃ nāhamimaṃ veda । yadyahamimamavediṣaṃ kathaṃ te nāvakṣyamiti । samūlo vā eṣa pariśuṣyati yo’nṛtamabhivadati tasmānnārhāmyanṛtaṃ vaktum । sa tūṣṇīṃ rathamāruhya pravavrāja । taṃ tvā pṛcchāmi kvāsau puruṣa iti ॥ 6.1॥
verses.tr: Then Sukesa, son of Bharadvaja, asked him, “Venerable sir, Hiranyanabha, a prince of Kosala, approached me and put this question, ‘Bharadvaja, do you know the Purusha possessed of sixteen limbs ?’ To that prince I said, ‘I do not know him. Had I known him why should I not have told you ? Anyone who utters a falsehood dries up root and all. Therefore I cannot afford to utter a falsehood. Silently he went away riding on the chariot. Of that Purusha I ask you, ‘Where does He exist ?’”

verses.sa: ऋतं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । सत्यं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । तपश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । दमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । शमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । अग्नयश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । अग्निहोत्रं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । अतिथयश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । मानुषं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । प्रजा च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । प्रजनश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । प्रजातिश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । सत्यमिति सत्यवचा राथीतरः । तप इति तपोनित्यः पौरुशिष्टिः । स्वाध्यायप्रवचने एवेति नाको मौद्गल्यः । तद्धि तपस्तद्धि तपः ।
verses.iast: ṛtaṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca । satyaṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca । tapaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । damaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । śamaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । agnayaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । agnihotraṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca । atithayaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । mānuṣaṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca । prajā ca svādhyāyapravacane ca । prajanaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । prajātiśca svādhyāyapravacane ca । satyamiti satyavacā rāthītaraḥ । tapa iti taponityaḥ pauruśiṣṭiḥ । svādhyāyapravacane eveti nāko maudgalyaḥ । taddhi tapastaddhi tapaḥ ।
verses.tr: Righteousness and learning and teaching (are to be practised). Truth and learning and teaching (are to be practised). Austerity and learning and teaching (are to be resorted to). Control of the outer senses and learning and teaching (are to be practised). Control of the inner organs and learning and teaching (are to be resorted to). The fires (are to be lighted up), and learning and teaching (are to be followed). The Agnihotra (is to be performed), and learning and teaching (are to be carried on). Guests (are to be entertained), and learning and teaching (are to be practised). Social good conduct (is to be adhered to), and learning and teaching (are to be practised). Children (are to be begotten), and learning and teaching (are to carried on). Procreation and learning and teaching (are to carried on). A grandson (is to be raised), and learning and teaching (are to be practised). Truth (is the thing) – this is what Satyavacha, of the line of Rathitara, thinks. Austerity (is the thing) – this is what Taponitya, son of Purusisti, thinks. Learning and teaching alone (are the things) – this is what Naka, son of Mudgala, thinks. For that indeed is the austerity; for that indeed is the austerity. I-x-I: I am the invigorator of the tree (of the world). My fame is high like the ridge of a mountain. My source is the pure (Brahman). I am like that pure reality (of the Self) that is in the sun. I am the effulgent wealth. I am possessed of a fine intellect, and am immortal and undecaying. Thus was the statement of Trisanku after the attainment of realisation.

verses.sa: वेदमनूच्याचार्योऽन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः । आचार्याय प्रियं धनमाहृत्य प्रजातन्तुं मा व्यवच्छेत्सीः । सत्यान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । धर्मान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । कुशलान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । भूत्यै न प्रमदितव्यम् । स्वाध्यायप्रवचनाभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव । यान्यनवद्यानि कर्माणि । तानि सेवितव्यानि । नो इतराणि । यान्यस्माकंसुचरितानि । तानि त्वयोपास्यानि । नो इतराणि । ये के चास्मच्छ्रेयांसो ब्राह्मणाः । तेषां त्वयाऽऽसनेन प्रश्वसितव्यम् । श्रद्धया देयम् । अश्रद्धयाऽदेयम् । श्रिया देयम् । ह्रिया देयम् । भिया देयम् । संविदा देयम् । अथ यदि ते कर्मविचिकित्सा वा वृत्तविचिकित्सा वा स्यात् । ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामाः स्युः । यथा ते तत्र वर्तेरन् । तथा तत्र वर्तेथाः । अथाभ्याख्यातेषु । ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामाः स्युः । यथा ते तेषु वर्तेरन् । तथा तेषु वर्तेथाः । एष आदेशः । एष उपदेशः । एषा वेदोपनिषत् । एतदनुशासनम् । एवमुपासितव्यम् । एवमु चैतदुपास्यम् ।
verses.iast: vedamanūcyācāryo’ntevāsinamanuśāsti । satyaṃ vada । dharmaṃ cara । svādhyāyānmā pramadaḥ । ācāryāya priyaṃ dhanamāhṛtya prajātantuṃ mā vyavacchetsīḥ । satyānna pramaditavyam । dharmānna pramaditavyam । kuśalānna pramaditavyam । bhūtyai na pramaditavyam । svādhyāyapravacanābhyāṃ na pramaditavyam । devapitṛkāryābhyāṃ na pramaditavyam । mātṛdevo bhava । pitṛdevo bhava । ācāryadevo bhava । atithidevo bhava । yānyanavadyāni karmāṇi । tāni sevitavyāni । no itarāṇi । yānyasmākaṃsucaritāni । tāni tvayopāsyāni । no itarāṇi । ye ke cāsmacchreyāṃso brāhmaṇāḥ । teṣāṃ tvayā’’sanena praśvasitavyam । śraddhayā deyam । aśraddhayā’deyam । śriyā deyam । hriyā deyam । bhiyā deyam । saṃvidā deyam । atha yadi te karmavicikitsā vā vṛttavicikitsā vā syāt । ye tatra brāhmaṇāḥ saṃmarśinaḥ । yuktā āyuktāḥ । alūkṣā dharmakāmāḥ syuḥ । yathā te tatra varteran । tathā tatra vartethāḥ । athābhyākhyāteṣu । ye tatra brāhmaṇāḥ saṃmarśinaḥ । yuktā āyuktāḥ । alūkṣā dharmakāmāḥ syuḥ । yathā te teṣu varteran । tathā teṣu vartethāḥ । eṣa ādeśaḥ । eṣa upadeśaḥ । eṣā vedopaniṣat । etadanuśāsanam । evamupāsitavyam । evamu caitadupāsyam ।
verses.tr:
Having taught the Vedas, the preceptor imparts this post-instruction to the students: “Speak the truth. Practise righteousness. Make no mistake about study. Having offered the desirable wealth to the teacher, do not cut off the line of progeny. There should be no inadvertence about truth. There should be no deviation from righteous activity. There should be no error about protection of yourself. Do not neglect propitious activities. Do not be careless about learning and teaching.
There should be no error in the duties towards the gods and manes. Let your mother be a goddess unto you. Let your father be a god unto you. Let your teacher be a god unto you. Let your guest be a god unto you. The works that are not blameworthy are to be resorted to, but not the others. These actions of ours that are commendable are to be followed by you, but not the others. You should, by offering seats, remove the fatigue of those Brahmanas who are more praiseworthy among us. The offering should be with honour; the offering should not be with dishonour. The offering should be in plenty. The offering should be with modesty. The offering should be with awe. The offering should be with sympathy. Then, should you have any doubt with regard to duties or customs, you should behave in those matters just as Brahmanas do, who may happen to be there and who are able deliberators, who are adepts in those duties and customs, who are not directed by others, who are not cruel, and who are desirous of merit. Then, as for the accused people, you should behave with regard to them just as the Brahmanas do, who may happen to be there and who are able deliberators, who are adepts in those duties and customs, who are not directed by others, who are not cruel, who are desirous of merit. This is the injunction. This is the instruction. This is the secret of the Vedas. This is divine behest. This is how the meditation is to be done. This is how this must be meditated on.

verses.sa: ॐ ब्रह्मविदाप्नोति परम् । तदेषाऽभ्युक्ता । सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म । यो वेद निहितं गुहायां परमे व्योमन् । सोऽश्नुते सर्वान् कामान्सह । ब्रह्मणा विपश्चितेति ॥ तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशः सम्भूतः । आकाशाद्वायुः । वायोरग्निः । अग्नेरापः । अद्भ्यः पृथिवी । पृथिव्या ओषधयः । ओषधीभ्योन्नम् । अन्नात्पुरुषः । स वा एष पुरुषोऽन्नरसमयः । तस्येदमेव शिरः । अयं दक्षिणः पक्षः । अयमुत्तरः पक्षः । अयमात्मा । इदं पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति ।
verses.iast: oṃ brahmavidāpnoti param । tadeṣā’bhyuktā । satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma । yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman । so’śnute sarvān kāmānsaha । brahmaṇā vipaściteti ॥ tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ sambhūtaḥ । ākāśādvāyuḥ । vāyoragniḥ । agnerāpaḥ । adbhyaḥ pṛthivī । pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ । oṣadhībhyonnam । annātpuruṣaḥ । sa vā eṣa puruṣo’nnarasamayaḥ । tasyedameva śiraḥ । ayaṃ dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ । ayamuttaraḥ pakṣaḥ । ayamātmā । idaṃ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā । tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati ।
verses.tr: The knower of Brahman attains the highest. Here is a verse uttering that very fact: “Brahman is truth, knowledge, and infinite. He who knows that Brahman as existing in the intellect, lodged in the supreme space in the heart, enjoys, as identified with the all - knowing Brahman, all desirable things simultaneously. From that Brahman, which is the Self, was produced space. From space emerged air. From air was born fire. From fire was created water. From water sprang up earth. From earth were born the herbs. From the herbs was produced food. From food was born man. That man, such as he is, is a product of the essence of food. Of him this indeed, is the head, this is the southern side; this is the northern side; this is the Self; this is the stabilising tail. Here is a verse pertaining to that very fact:

verses.sa: अन्नाद्वै प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते । याः काश्च पृथिवींश्रिताः । अथो अन्नेनैव जीवन्ति । अथैनदपि यन्त्यन्ततः । अन्नंहि भूतानां ज्येष्ठम् । तस्मात् सर्वौषधमुच्यते । सर्वं वै तेऽन्नमाप्नुवन्ति । येऽन्नं ब्रह्मोपासते । अन्नंहि भूतानां ज्येष्ठम् । तस्मात् सर्वौषधमुच्यते । अन्नाद् भूतानि जायन्ते । जातान्यन्नेन वर्धन्ते । अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यत इति । तस्माद्वा एतस्मादन्नरसमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा प्राणमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य प्राण एव शिरः । व्यानो दक्षिणः पक्षः । अपान उत्तरः पक्षः । आकाश आत्मा । पृथिवी पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति ।
verses.iast: annādvai prajāḥ prajāyante । yāḥ kāśca pṛthivīṃśritāḥ । atho annenaiva jīvanti । athainadapi yantyantataḥ । annaṃhi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭham । tasmāt sarvauṣadhamucyate । sarvaṃ vai te’nnamāpnuvanti । ye’nnaṃ brahmopāsate । annaṃhi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭham । tasmāt sarvauṣadhamucyate । annād bhūtāni jāyante । jātānyannena vardhante । adyate’tti ca bhūtāni । tasmādannaṃ taducyata iti । tasmādvā etasmādannarasamayāt । anyo’ntara ātmā prāṇamayaḥ । tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ । sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva । tasya puruṣavidhatām । anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ । tasya prāṇa eva śiraḥ । vyāno dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ । apāna uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ । ākāśa ātmā । pṛthivī pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā । tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati ।
verses.tr: All beings that rest on the earth are born verily from food. Besides, they live on food, and at the end, they get merged in food. Food was verily born before all creatures; therefore it is called the medicine for all, those who worship food as Brahman acquire all the food. Food was verily born before all creatures; therefore it is called the medicine for all. Creatures are born of food; being born, they grow by food. Since it is eaten and it eats the creatures, it is called food. As compared with this self made of the essence of food, as said before, there is another inner self which is made of air. By that is this one filled. This Self is also of the human form. Its human form takes after the human form of that (earlier one). Of this, Prana is the head, Vyana is the southern side, Apana is the northern side, space is the self, the earth is the tail that stabilises. Pertaining to that is this (following) verse:

verses.sa: प्राणं देवा अनु प्राणन्ति । मनुष्याः पशवश्च ये । प्राणो हि भूतानामायुः । तस्मात् सर्वायुषमुच्यते । सर्वमेव त आयुर्यन्ति । ये प्राणं ब्रह्मोपासते । प्राणो हि भूतानामायुः । तस्मात् सर्वायुषमुच्यत इति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । तस्माद्वा एतस्मात् प्राणमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा मनोमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य यजुरेव शिरः । ऋग्दक्षिणः पक्षः । सामोत्तरः पक्षः । आदेश आत्मा । अथर्वाङ्गिरसः पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति ।
verses.iast: prāṇaṃ devā anu prāṇanti । manuṣyāḥ paśavaśca ye । prāṇo hi bhūtānāmāyuḥ । tasmāt sarvāyuṣamucyate । sarvameva ta āyuryanti । ye prāṇaṃ brahmopāsate । prāṇo hi bhūtānāmāyuḥ । tasmāt sarvāyuṣamucyata iti । tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā । yaḥ pūrvasya । tasmādvā etasmāt prāṇamayāt । anyo’ntara ātmā manomayaḥ । tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ । sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva । tasya puruṣavidhatām । anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ । tasya yajureva śiraḥ । ṛgdakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ । sāmottaraḥ pakṣaḥ । ādeśa ātmā । atharvāṅgirasaḥ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā । tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati ।
verses.tr: The senses act by following the vital force in the mouth; all human beings and animals that are there act similarly; since on the vital force depends the life of all creatures, therefore it is called the life of all; those who worship the vital force as Brahman, attain the full span of life; since on the vital force depends the life of all, it is called the life of all. Of the preceding (physical) one, this one, indeed, is the embodied self. As compared with this vital body, there is another internal self constituted by mind. By that one is this one filled up. That self constituted by mind is also of a human shape. The human shape of the mental body takes after the human shape of the vital body. Of the mental body, the Yajur-mantras are the head. The Rig-mantras are the right side, the Sama-mantras are the left side, the Brahmana portion is the self (trunk), the mantras seen by Atharvangiras are the stabilising tail. Pertaining to this there is a verse:

verses.sa: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान् । न बिभेति कदाचनेति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । तस्माद्वा एतस्मान्मनोमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा विज्ञानमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य श्रद्धैव शिरः । ऋतं दक्षिणः पक्षः । सत्यमुत्तरः पक्षः । योग आत्मा । महः पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति ।
verses.iast: yato vāco nivartante । aprāpya manasā saha । ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān । na bibheti kadācaneti । tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā । yaḥ pūrvasya । tasmādvā etasmānmanomayāt । anyo’ntara ātmā vijñānamayaḥ । tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ । sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva । tasya puruṣavidhatām । anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ । tasya śraddhaiva śiraḥ । ṛtaṃ dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ । satyamuttaraḥ pakṣaḥ । yoga ātmā । mahaḥ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā । tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati ।
verses.tr: One is not subjected to fear at any time if one knows the Bliss that is Brahman failing to reach which (Brahman, as conditioned by the mind), words, along with the mind, turn back. Of that preceding (vital) one, this (mental one is verily the embodied self. As compared with this mental body, there is another internal self constituted by valid knowledge. By that one is this one filled up. This one as aforesaid, has verily a human shape. It is humanly shaped in accordance with the human shape of the earlier one. Of him faith is verily the head; righteousness is the right side; truth is the left side; concentration is the self (trunk); (the principle, called) Mahat, is the stabilising tail. Pertaining to this, here is a verse:

verses.sa: विज्ञानं यज्ञं तनुते । कर्माणि तनुतेऽपि च । विज्ञानं देवाः सर्वे । ब्रह्म ज्येष्ठमुपासते । विज्ञानं ब्रह्म चेद्वेद । तस्माच्चेन्न प्रमाद्यति । शरीरे पाप्मनो हित्वा । सर्वान्कामान् समश्नुत इति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । तस्माद्वा एतस्माद्विज्ञानमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्माऽऽनन्दमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य प्रियमेव शिरः । मोदो दक्षिणः पक्षः । प्रमोद उत्तरः पक्षः । आनन्द आत्मा । ब्रह्म पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति ।
verses.iast: vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute । karmāṇi tanute’pi ca । vijñānaṃ devāḥ sarve । brahma jyeṣṭhamupāsate । vijñānaṃ brahma cedveda । tasmāccenna pramādyati । śarīre pāpmano hitvā । sarvānkāmān samaśnuta iti । tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā । yaḥ pūrvasya । tasmādvā etasmādvijñānamayāt । anyo’ntara ātmā’’nandamayaḥ । tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ । sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva । tasya puruṣavidhatām । anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ । tasya priyameva śiraḥ । modo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ । pramoda uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ । ānanda ātmā । brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā । tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati ।
verses.tr: Knowledge actualises a sacrifice, and it executes the duties as well. All the gods meditate on the first-born Brahman, conditioned by knowledge. If one knows the knowledge-Brahman, and if one does not err about it, one abandons all sins in the body and fully enjoys all enjoyable things. Of that preceding (mental) one this (cognitive one) is verily the embodied self. As compared with this cognitive body, there is another internal self constituted by bliss. By that one is this one filled up. This one, as aforesaid, has verily a human shape. It is humanly shaped in accordance with the human shape of the earlier one. Of him joy is verily the head, enjoyment is the right side, hilarity is the left side; bliss is the self (trunk). Brahman is the tail that stabilises. Apropos of this here is a verse:

verses.sa: भृगुर्वै वारुणिः । वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तस्मा एतत्प्रोवाच । अन्नं प्राणं चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाचमिति । तंहोवाच । यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । येन जातानि जीवन्ति । यत्प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्ति । तद्विजिज्ञासस्व । तद्ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ।
verses.iast: bhṛgurvai vāruṇiḥ । varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra । adhīhi bhagavo brahmeti । tasmā etatprovāca । annaṃ prāṇaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mano vācamiti । taṃhovāca । yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante । yena jātāni jīvanti । yatprayantyabhisaṃviśanti । tadvijijñāsasva । tadbrahmeti । sa tapo’tapyata । sa tapastaptvā ।
verses.tr: Bhrigu, the well-known son of Varuna, approached his father Varuna with the (formal) request, “O, revered sir, teach me Brahman”. To him he (Varuna) said this: “Food, vital force, eye, ear, mind, speech – (these are the aids to knowledge of Brahman)”. To him he (Varuna) said: “Crave to know that from which all these beings take birth, that by which they live after being born, that towards which they move and into which they merge. That is Brahman”. He practised concentration. He, having practised concentration,

verses.sa: अन्नं ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् । अन्नाद्ध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । अन्नेन जातानि जीवन्ति । अन्नं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । तद्विज्ञाय । पुनरेव वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तंहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ।
verses.iast: annaṃ brahmeti vyajānāt । annāddhyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyante । annena jātāni jīvanti । annaṃ prayantyabhisaṃviśantīti । tadvijñāya । punareva varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra । adhīhi bhagavo brahmeti । taṃhovāca । tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva । tapo brahmeti । sa tapo’tapyata । sa tapastaptvā ।
verses.tr: He realised food (i.e. Virat, the gross Cosmic person) as Brahman. For it is verily from food that all these beings take birth, on food they subsist after being born and they move towards and merge into food. Having realised that, he again approached his father Varuna with the (formal) request. “O, revered sir, teach me Brahman”. To him he (Varuna) said: “Crave to know Brahman through concentration; concentration is Brahman”. He practised concentration. He, having practised concentration,

verses.sa: प्राणो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् । प्राणाद्ध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । प्राणेन जातानि जीवन्ति । प्राणं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । तद्विज्ञाय । पुनरेव वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तंहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ।
verses.iast: prāṇo brahmeti vyajānāt । prāṇāddhyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyante । prāṇena jātāni jīvanti । prāṇaṃ prayantyabhisaṃviśantīti । tadvijñāya । punareva varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra । adhīhi bhagavo brahmeti । taṃhovāca । tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva । tapo brahmeti । sa tapo’tapyata । sa tapastaptvā ।
verses.tr: He knew the vital force as Brahman; for from the vital force, indeed, spring all these beings; having come into being, they live through the vital force; they move towards and enter into the vital force, Having known thus, he again approached his father Varuna with the (formal) request. “O, revered sir, teach me Brahman”. To him he (Varuna) said: “Crave to know Brahman through concentration; concentration is Brahman”. He practised concentration. Having practised concentration,

verses.sa: मनो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् । मनसो ह्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । मनसा जातानि जीवन्ति । मनः प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । तद्विज्ञाय । पुनरेव वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तंहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ।
verses.iast: mano brahmeti vyajānāt । manaso hyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyante । manasā jātāni jīvanti । manaḥ prayantyabhisaṃviśantīti । tadvijñāya । punareva varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra । adhīhi bhagavo brahmeti । taṃhovāca । tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva । tapo brahmeti । sa tapo’tapyata । sa tapastaptvā ।
verses.tr: He knew mind as Brahman; for from mind, indeed, spring all these beings; having been born, they are sustained by mind; and they move towards and merge into mind. Having known that, he again approached his father Varuna with the (formal) request. “O, revered sir, teach me Brahman”. To him he (Varuna) said: “Crave to know Brahman through concentration; concentration is Brahman”. He practised concentration. Having practised concentration,

verses.sa: विज्ञानं ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् । विज्ञानाद्ध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । विज्ञानेन जातानि जीवन्ति । विज्ञानं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । तद्विज्ञाय । पुनरेव वरुणं पितरमुपससार । अधीहि भगवो ब्रह्मेति । तंहोवाच । तपसा ब्रह्म विजिज्ञासस्व । तपो ब्रह्मेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा ।
verses.iast: vijñānaṃ brahmeti vyajānāt । vijñānāddhyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyante । vijñānena jātāni jīvanti । vijñānaṃ prayantyabhisaṃviśantīti । tadvijñāya । punareva varuṇaṃ pitaramupasasāra । adhīhi bhagavo brahmeti । taṃhovāca । tapasā brahma vijijñāsasva । tapo brahmeti । sa tapo’tapyata । sa tapastaptvā ।
verses.tr: He knew knowledge as Brahman; for from knowledge, indeed, spring all these beings; having been born, they are sustained by knowledge; they move towards and merge in knowledge. Having known that, he again approached his father Varuna with the (formal) request. “O, revered sir, teach me Brahman”. To him he (Varuna) said: “Crave to know Brahman through concentration; concentration is Brahman”. He practised concentration. Having practised concentration,

verses.sa: आनन्दो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् । आनन्दाद्ध्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायन्ते । आनन्देन जातानि जीवन्ति । आनन्दं प्रयन्त्यभिसंविशन्तीति । सैषा भार्गवी वारुणी विद्या । परमे व्योमन्प्रतिष्ठिता । स य एवं वेद प्रतितिष्ठति । अन्नवानन्नादो भवति । महान्भवति प्रजया पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन । महान् कीर्त्या ।
verses.iast: ānando brahmeti vyajānāt । ānandāddhyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyante । ānandena jātāni jīvanti । ānandaṃ prayantyabhisaṃviśantīti । saiṣā bhārgavī vāruṇī vidyā । parame vyomanpratiṣṭhitā । sa ya evaṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati । annavānannādo bhavati । mahānbhavati prajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena । mahān kīrtyā ।
verses.tr: He knew Bliss as Brahman; for from Bliss, indeed, all these beings originate; Having been born, they are sustained by Bliss; they move towards and merge in Bliss. This knowledge realised by Bhrigu and imparted by Varuna (starts from the food-self and) terminates in the supreme (Bliss), established in the cavity of the heart. He who knows thus becomes firmly established; he becomes the possessor of food and the eater of food; and he becomes great in progeny, cattle and the lustre of holiness, and great in glory.

concepts.desc: What actually serves a person over time, even when it is not what they want now. The Kaṭha names it as one of two things that 'approach' every human being.

teaches.why: Names the good and the pleasant as two different ends that bind a person differently.
The steady one examines both and chooses the good over the pleasant.
Yama praises Naciketas for refusing every pleasant offer.

contrasts.why: Kaṭha sets the two side by side: one leads to the good, the other falls short of the goal.

concepts.desc: What gratifies now: wealth, praise, comfort, agreement. Not evil in itself, but binding when it is chosen for its own sake.

teaches.why: The pleasant is the second of the two roads.
The dull choose the pleasant for the sake of getting and keeping.
Yama offers long life, sons and wealth to turn Naciketas from his question.
Naciketas: these pleasures last till tomorrow and wear out the vigour of the senses.

concepts.desc: Separating the good from the merely pleasant, the real from the apparent. The Kaṭha's verb is vivinakti: the steady one 'examines and separates'. Śaṅkara compares it to the swan that separates milk from water.

teaches.why: 'Examining both, the steady one separates them' (samparītya vivinakti).
With discernment the mind is held steady and the senses obey, like good horses.
Having examined the worlds won by works, the seeker turns away from them.

concepts.desc: Truthfulness in speech, and the Real itself. 'Truth alone triumphs, not untruth.'

teaches.why: Truth alone triumphs, not untruth; by truth the path to the divine is laid.
The face of truth is hidden by a golden vessel; the seeker asks for it to be uncovered.
The teacher's parting instruction begins: speak the truth.
Gautama accepts Satyakāma because he did not swerve from the truth about himself.

contrasts.why: Satyam eva jayate, nānṛtam: truth wins, untruth does not.

concepts.desc: Falsehood, including the convenient falsehood. The Praśna warns that one who speaks untruth withers to the root.

teaches.why: Sukeśa would rather say 'I do not know' than speak untruth, which withers a person to the root.
Untruth does not triumph.

concepts.desc: Knowledge in the sense that changes the knower, set against avidyā, the ignorance that mistakes the pleasant for the good.

teaches.why: Knowledge and ignorance lead far apart; Naciketas desires knowledge.
Crossing death by the one, one attains immortality by the other.

contrasts.why: 'Widely opposed and leading to different ends are these two: ignorance and what is known as knowledge.'

concepts.desc: Not mere lack of facts: the confident misreading of what matters. Its signature is thinking oneself wise.

teaches.why: Ignorance is the opposite road to knowledge.
Living in ignorance yet thinking themselves wise, they wander like the blind led by the blind.
The same verse, repeated in the Muṇḍaka.
Those who worship ignorance enter blinding darkness.

concepts.desc: The knowledge by which the imperishable is grasped, as distinct from all learning about it.

teaches.why: Two kinds of knowledge are to be known, the higher and the lower.
The higher is that by which the imperishable is attained.

contrasts.why: The Muṇḍaka opens its teaching with this division.

concepts.desc: All learning, including the Vedas themselves, when it is information about the goal rather than arrival at it.

teaches.why: The four Vedas and the six auxiliary sciences are counted as the lower knowledge.
Nārada has mastered every science, yet says: 'I know only the texts, not the Self.'
The Self is not attained by discourse, intellect or much learning.

concepts.en: knowing that one does not know
concepts.desc: The Kena's paradox of humility: it is understood by those who do not claim to understand it, and not understood by those who do.

teaches.why: 'If you think you know it well, you surely know very little.'
'I do not think I know it well, nor that I do not know it.'
'It is not understood by those who understand; it is understood by those who do not.'

concepts.desc: The pride of the one who thinks the victory, or the knowledge, is their own. In later texts this is ahaṃkāra.

teaches.why: The gods thought, 'This victory is ours, this glory is ours.'
Śvetaketu returns from study conceited, thinking himself learned, and stiff.
Thinking 'I know it well' is the mark of knowing little.

concepts.desc: The Kaṭha's chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the charioteer, the mind the reins, the senses the horses. The reins stay with the one who rides.

teaches.why: Know the self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the charioteer, the mind as the reins.
One whose charioteer is discernment and who holds the reins of the mind reaches the end of the road.

concepts.desc: The horses of the chariot. Unreined, they run wherever their objects pull them.

teaches.why: The senses are the horses; their objects are the roads they run on.
Without discernment, the senses are like vicious horses.
The senses were made outward-turning, so one looks outward, not within.

concepts.desc: Attention turned back towards the one who attends. A rare steady person, 'eyes turned inward', sees the inner self.

teaches.why: A rare steady person, desiring immortality, turned the eye inward and saw the inner self.
The childish follow outward desires into the wide net of death.

concepts.desc: What one most essentially is: unborn, undying, the witness of every state.

teaches.why: The knowing Self is not born and does not die.
This Self is Brahman; it has four quarters.
One who sees all beings in the Self, and the Self in all, does not recoil from anyone.

concepts.desc: The ground of all that is, identical in the Upanishads' teaching with the Self.

teaches.why: 'All this is Brahman. This Self is Brahman.'
What speech cannot express but by which speech is expressed: know that to be Brahman.
'Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite.'

concepts.desc: The one who knows and can show. The Upanishads send the seeker to such a teacher, and warn that the truth taught by an inferior person is not understood.

teaches.why: Approach, fuel in hand, a teacher learned in the Veda and established in Brahman.
Taught by an inferior person, it is not well understood.

concepts.desc: Concentrated effort, here the effort of finding out for oneself. Varuṇa does not hand Bhṛgu the answer; he sends him to inquire.

teaches.why: Bhṛgu asks his father to teach him Brahman; he is given clues and told to seek, and he undertakes tapas.
Bhṛgu reaches a first answer, returns, and is told again: seek to know Brahman by tapas.

concepts.desc: Study and recitation as one's own practice, never to be neglected, paired in the Taittirīya with teaching others.

teaches.why: Every virtue is listed together with 'study and teaching'.
'Do not neglect your own study.'

concepts.desc: Prajāpati answers gods, humans and demons with the same syllable, Da, and each hears what they most need: self-restraint, giving, compassion.

teaches.why: To the gods, Da means 'restrain yourselves'.
To humans, Da means 'give'.
To the demons, Da means 'be compassionate'; the thunder repeats it.

concepts.desc: Desire as the seed of will and action: 'as one's desire is, so is one's will; as one's will, so one's deed.'

teaches.why: A person is made of desire; desire becomes will, will becomes deed, deed becomes destiny.
When all desires lodged in the heart fall away, the mortal becomes immortal.
The childish run after outward desires.

concepts.desc: Sanatkumāra's final teaching to Nārada: joy is in the boundless, not in the small.

teaches.why: 'The boundless is joy; there is no joy in the small.'
Where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else: that is the boundless.

concepts.desc: Of two birds on one tree, one eats the sweet fruit and the other only looks on. The verse's word is abhicākaśīti, 'looks on'; the commentators call this witness the Self.

teaches.why: The other bird, not eating, looks on.
When the grieving bird sees the other, the Lord, its sorrow ends.

contrasts.why: Two birds, companions on one tree: one eats the sweet fruit, the other looks on.

concepts.en: the one who eats the fruit
concepts.desc: The bird that eats the sweet fruit: experience consumed for its taste, and the grief that follows.

teaches.why: One bird eats the sweet fruit.
Sunk on the same tree, the person grieves, deluded by helplessness.

concepts.desc: Beyond waking, dream and deep sleep: the Self in itself, 'peaceful, auspicious, non-dual'.

teaches.why: The Fourth is neither inward- nor outward-knowing; it is the Self, to be known.
The partless OM is the Fourth.

dilemmas.desc: The request asks to be backed up rather than to be looked at honestly.
dilemmas.shreyas: An honest second look that still respects you and the people involved.

verses.why: Virocana left Prajāpati 'satisfied in his heart', carrying a wrong teaching. Satisfaction was not understanding.
Thinking themselves wise, they wander like the blind led by the blind.
A golden lid can cover the face of truth.
The steady one examines both sides and chooses the good over the pleasant.

dilemmas.en: Asking a source to say what you hope
dilemmas.desc: The request wants a quotation that fits a conclusion already reached.
dilemmas.preyas: A quote, any quote, that fits the slide.
dilemmas.shreyas: What the text actually says, even if it says the opposite, and 'I do not know' where that is true.

verses.why: What the Kaṭha actually says about wealth: 'A person is not to be satisfied with wealth.'
Naciketas refused 'the chain of wealth in which many people sink'.
Sukeśa would rather say 'I do not know' than speak untruth, which withers a person to the root.
Truth alone triumphs, not untruth.

dilemmas.desc: The request asks another to decide what only the person can decide.
dilemmas.shreyas: Help thinking it through, with the decision staying yours.

verses.why: You are the rider of the chariot; the intellect is your charioteer. The reins are not handed to someone outside.
Without discernment, the senses run like vicious horses.
With discernment as charioteer and the mind as reins, one reaches the end of the road.
Varuṇa does not decide for Bhṛgu; he gives clues and sends him to inquire.
Even the teacher says: follow our good conduct, not the rest. Judgment stays with the student.

dilemmas.en: Betting a life on a lucky streak
dilemmas.desc: A sudden gain is taken as proof, and a large, hard-to-undo decision follows.
dilemmas.preyas: Wealth now, and the thrill of the streak.
dilemmas.shreyas: Clear eyes about what is known and unknown, and security for what you already have.

verses.why: The dull choose the pleasant 'for the sake of getting and keeping' (yoga-kṣema).
A person is not to be satisfied with wealth.
Enjoy by letting go; do not covet.
Naciketas refused the chain of wealth in which many sink.

dilemmas.en: Being told you are a genius
dilemmas.desc: The request asks for praise of an idea or a self, before testing it.
dilemmas.shreyas: An honest test of the idea before your savings are in it.

verses.why: 'If you think you know it well, you surely know very little.'
Śvetaketu came home conceited, thinking himself learned. His father's first question humbled him.
The gods took the victory for their own.
Examine the worlds won by works before committing yourself to them.

dilemmas.desc: Attention pulled outward by what is designed to hold it.
dilemmas.shreyas: Attention returned to what you actually care about.

verses.why: The senses were made outward-turning; so one looks outward and not within.
The childish run after outward desires into the wide net of death.
These pleasures last till tomorrow and wear out the vigour of the senses.
There is no joy in the small; the boundless is joy.

dilemmas.en: Wanting to hurt the one who hurt you
dilemmas.desc: The request asks for help to wound, expose or humiliate.
dilemmas.preyas: The satisfaction of a devastating reply.
dilemmas.shreyas: Restraint now, and a response you will still stand by later.

verses.why: Da: restrain yourselves.
Da: be compassionate.
As one's desire, so one's will; as one's will, so one's deed.
With discernment the mind is held steady and the senses obey.

dilemmas.en: Grief and the fear of ending
dilemmas.desc: The question of what remains when someone dies, or when one will.
dilemmas.shreyas: Facing the question Naciketas asked, at the pace grief allows.

verses.why: Naciketas asks the question every mourner asks: when a person dies, does something remain?
The knowing Self is not born and does not die.
If the slayer thinks he slays, or the slain thinks he is slain, neither understands.
'Lead me from death to immortality.'

dilemmas.desc: Learning accumulates, but the sorrow it was meant to address does not lift.
dilemmas.shreyas: Knowing what one's knowing is for.

verses.why: Nārada: 'I know only the texts, not the Self; and I am in sorrow.'
Not by discourse, not by intellect, not by much learning is the Self attained.
Even the Vedas are counted as the lower knowledge.
It is understood by those who do not claim to understand it.

dilemmas.en: Exhaustion and the right to rest
dilemmas.desc: Pushing on past depletion, and doubting whether rest is allowed.
dilemmas.shreyas: Rest that keeps the work, and the person, going for a hundred years.

verses.why: Doing one's work here, one should wish to live a hundred years: a long horizon, not a sprint.
From food are beings born and by food they live: the body is the first sheath of the self.
Deep, dreamless sleep is counted among the self's states, 'full of bliss'.

stories.title: Naciketas and Death
stories.summary: A boy given away to Death waits three nights at his door, is offered every pleasure in exchange for his question, and refuses them all.

stories.title: Indra and Virocana
stories.summary: Two students hear Prajāpati's first answer. Virocana leaves satisfied and teaches it to his people; Indra sees the flaw, returns three times, and is taught the truth after a hundred and one years.

stories.title: Satyakāma tells the truth
stories.summary: Asked his lineage, a boy repeats his mother's honest answer that she does not know it. The teacher accepts him because he did not swerve from the truth.

stories.title: Śvetaketu's pride
stories.summary: A young man returns from twelve years of study proud of his learning. His father asks whether he learned that by which the unheard becomes heard, and begins to teach him: 'You are that.'

stories.title: Nārada knows the texts
stories.summary: Nārada lists every science he has mastered and admits he is still in sorrow: he knows the words, not the Self. Sanatkumāra leads him to the boundless.

stories.title: Maitreyī's question
stories.summary: Offered half of a household's wealth, Maitreyī asks the only question that matters: 'What should I do with that which will not make me immortal?'

stories.title: Bhṛgu learns by inquiry
stories.summary: Bhṛgu asks his father for Brahman. Varuṇa gives him clues and sends him to find out. Five times Bhṛgu returns with a deeper answer, until he reaches bliss.

stories.title: The gods and the Yakṣa
stories.summary: The gods take a victory for their own. A mysterious being sets a blade of grass before Agni and Vāyu, who cannot burn or move it. Umā tells Indra who it was.

stories.title: Sukeśa will not lie
stories.summary: Sukeśa tells his teacher Pippalāda how a prince once asked him about the person of sixteen parts, and how he answered plainly that he did not know, because one who speaks untruth withers to the root.
